market.question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: According to IMF PortWatch, Bab el-Mandeb traffic averaged 28 vessels/day in August 2026, the lowest monthly level in the recent series. A 3-day sample to about 11 September averaged about 26/day (79 vessels), and the 7-day moving average was 24/day on 29 July.

A late-September update said IMF PortWatch recorded a single transit for 20 September, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85/day. It did not say whether this was a preliminary or lagged figure, and it gave no 7-day average. Neither the figure nor which strait it refers to has been checked against PortWatch.

recent_facts.source: Search summary of late-September shipping reports (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Reports summarized in search results said IMF PortWatch AIS data for Bab el-Mandeb in mid-to-late September 2026 showed daily volumes in the low-to-mid 20s, with about 22 vessels on recent days. This has not been checked against the PortWatch page itself.

Lloyd's List Intelligence's own Red Sea Transit Monitor counted 290 preliminary Bab el-Mandeb transits for 21–27 September 2026 (264 the week before), a 4-week weekly average of 280, against 316 in June and 257 in January. This counting method differs from PortWatch's and gives higher numbers.
In early to mid September 2026, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast down to the Bab el-Mandeb, including the port of Mocha. Other reports say they also took Perim Island and the Hanish Islands.
Windward reported that Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from 35 daily transits before the Houthi advance to 25 after. Traffic then recovered, reaching 45 transits on one Sunday in mid-September.

The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in September 2026 and said Saudi shipping using the strait would be targeted. There have been 12 Houthi attacks or attempted attacks on commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea since July 2026.
The Houthis told the EU in a letter that they would not target European ships in the Red Sea and that their activity would not affect navigation through Bab el-Mandeb.

On 4 October 2026, the Saudi-led coalition pledged support for a Yemeni government offensive against the Houthis. ABC News reported the same day that the Houthis targeted a Saudi oil facility as hostilities escalated.

The Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia, imposed on 20 July 2026, reduced crude exports through the Yanbu terminals. The Saudi pipeline has resumed at reduced rates, and some operators are increasingly sending ships back through the Red Sea.
A Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb on 11 August 2026 killed four to six crew. The PortWatch monthly average stayed at 28/day for August.

recent_facts.source: Anadolu Agency (citing IMF PortWatch / World Bank)
recent_facts.fact: PortWatch daily averages: about 71/day from January 2022 to October 2023; 43/day from 17 November 2023 to 19 February 2024; about 33.5/day in 2025; 34–37/day in January–July 2026; 28/day in August 2026. None of the figures found here comes close to a 7-day average of 10 or below, including through the 2024–2025 Houthi campaign. This is not a full check of PortWatch's daily series.

The question resolves Yes if PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of Bab el-Mandeb transit calls of 10 or below for any date through 31 October 2026. PortWatch counts AIS-visible transits, so ships with AIS off are not counted. Revisions are considered only until the 31 October data is published.
PortWatch daily data is published with a lag. Data for dates up to 31 October must appear within 14 days after that date, and the question closes on 1 November 2026 (03:59 UTC).

market.question: Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement announced by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a ceasefire agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify. Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement. Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g. restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

All listed countries/parties must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for a Yes resolution. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a ceasefire agreement will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The East-West pipeline restarted on September 22, 2026 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd. The report rests on Reuters sources and does not cite any announcement from the Saudi government, the Ministry of Energy or SPA.

Saudi Aramco is reported to be pumping close to 6 million bpd through the 7 million bpd East-West pipeline, more than 80% of capacity, after the September 22 restart. The report notes that Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not respond to requests for comment, so no official confirmation is cited. Date approximate (early October).

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on September 10–11. The attacks hit the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing fires, some damage and injuries.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the Saudi pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. This is a US official speaking, not the Saudi government.

The 7 million bpd pipeline carries crude to Red Sea export terminals and has been Saudi Arabia's main way around Hormuz during the Iran war. Brent rose more than 3% to $108 after the shutdown. Later reports said Yanbu loadings had picked up, a sign the pipeline was running again.

Kendre Miller had 9 carries for 30 yards and 1 rushing TD in Week 1 against Detroit while working as RB3. He was a healthy inactive in Week 2 when Kamara came back from injury. Opposition Jewish bloc 52 (Yashar 21, Together 11, Democrats 11, Yisrael Beiteinu 9). Arab parties 14. Neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority.
Maariv poll: Netanyahu bloc 51 seats, opposition 53, Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 9. The Netanyahu bloc gained 2 seats from Maariv's previous poll and neither camp reaches 61.

Late-September polls disagree on Netanyahu's bloc total. Channel 14: 63 (Likud 32). i24NEWS: 60 (Likud 27). Zman Yisrael: 53. Channel 13: 51. N12: 50. Maariv: 49. Yashar is at 22-23 in most of them. The Reservists party is placed in different blocs by different pollsters, which moves bloc totals by several seats.

The election is set for October 27, 2026, after the Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026 at the end of its full term. The threshold is 3.25% and 61 of 120 seats are needed for a majority. Netanyahu is the incumbent PM and Likud's candidate, with New Hope merged into Likud.

The question resolves only on a PM formally sworn in after the 2026 election; a caretaker PM does not count. If Netanyahu stays on as caretaker during coalition talks, that is not a swearing-in. If nobody is sworn in by Dec 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The question closes Oct 28, 2026, one day after the vote.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: after the Nov 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu's government was sworn in on Dec 29, 2022, about 58 days later. Israeli government formation usually takes weeks to months, so no swearing-in would be expected by the Oct 28 close.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: of the 6 Knesset elections from 2015 to 2022, the PM sworn in directly after the vote was Netanyahu after 2015, 2020 and 2022, and Bennett after 2021. The April 2019 and Sept 2019 elections produced no government and led to repeat elections.

On Sept 23 the Central Elections Committee disqualified Ra'am and the Joint List. The Supreme Court overturned that on Oct 2, and on Oct 4 it rejected further disqualification appeals. Petitions against Otzma Yehudit were rejected on Sept 24.

Bennett said he is willing to give up the premiership in a post-Netanyahu government. The opposition Jewish parties (Yashar, Together, Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu) have said they won't form a coalition that includes Arab parties. Lieberman has not endorsed any PM candidate.

Election day is Oct 27, 2026. After that the President consults with parties and assigns a candidate to form a government, and the new government must win a Knesset vote and be sworn in. Under the question's rules, this has to happen by Dec 31, 2027.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: Faktor plus poll (Sept 16–20, n=986, about 62% expected turnout): United Serbia (SNS) 48.6%, Student List 37.1%, SPS 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8%, Mi snaga naroda 1.2%. 16% of respondents were undecided.
Faktor plus's earlier poll had SNS at 47.2% and Student List at 31.5%. In the next poll the Student List rose 5.6 points and SNS 1.4 points.

recent_facts.source: CRTA / Stanford Democracy Action Lab via Danas
recent_facts.fact: CRTA poll (June 10–24, face-to-face, n=2,324): among decided voters (about 70%), Student List 44.9%, SNS 35.7%, SPS 3.8%, and all others below the threshold. Wikipedia describes it as the first regular national poll since July 2010 with any option other than SNS in first place.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list PR in one nationwide constituency using D'Hondt, with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic minority lists. 126 seats are needed for a majority. Sixteen lists were registered, including United Serbia (SNS-led, headed by Vučić), SPS, European Serbia, Authentic Right (NADA) and the Student List (ballot holder Ilija Srdanović).

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as president on September 27, more than seven months before his term ended, after calling the snap election. Al Jazeera reported that polls suggest the race between his party and the student-backed list could be tight.
Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister at Belgrade's largest indoor arena, which thousands of supporters filled, and promised a 'comprehensive' victory.
Vučić dissolved the National Assembly on September 9 and called early elections for October 25, 2026, although the regular mandate ran to December 2027.

Students marched to register the 'Student List – Students Are Winning', a slate of 250 candidates. It is backed by many opposition parties, including DS, ZLF, Kreni-Promeni, SDS, LSV, Dveri and Enough is Enough. Some opposition parties are running separately, for example European Serbia (SSP and others).

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – 2023 Serbian parliamentary election (series count recalled from memory; unverified)
recent_facts.fact: In 2023 the SNS-led 'Serbia Must Not Stop' list won 129 of 250 seats. From memory, and not checked against a single cited source: an SNS-led list has won the most seats in each of the last 6 parliamentary elections (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023).
Polling coverage reports that about one in three voters had not finally decided whom to support.

Statements, interviews, social media posts, polls, jokes, or expressions of interest in renaming the company will not qualify unless accompanied by an official announcement that the name change has been adopted. Renaming any SpaceXAI or SpaceX product, model, division, subsidiary, or program (e.g., Grok, X), without renaming the company itself, will not qualify. market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

market.question: Will Saudi airspace be closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Saudi Arabian Airspace (The Jeddah Flight Information Region (FIR)/OEJD) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before market creation; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before market creation, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Saudi Arabian government, including the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), and Saudi Air Navigation Services (SANS), and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Faktor Plus via sd.rs / Wikipedia polling page
recent_facts.fact: Faktor Plus poll (Sept 16–20, 2026, 986 respondents) has 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' at 48.6% (+1.4 on the month) and the Student List at 37.1% (+5.6). SPS polled 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8% and Nestorović's list 1.2%. Expected turnout was about 62%, and 16% were undecided.

An NSPM (Nova srpska politička misao) poll from the first ten days of September 2026, published in Vreme on October 1, has the Student List at 44.3% and Vučić's list at 41.7%. The analyst Vukadinović notes that the fieldwork came before the election was called, before some parties withdrew to back the Student List, and before Nestorović's list was eliminated.

Earlier Faktor Plus polls had SNS well ahead: 46.4% vs 28.7% in April, 47.1% vs 30.7% in June, and 47.2% vs 31.5% in early September 2026 (n=1,200). Faktor Plus has had SNS first in every poll, while CRTA and NSPM have had the Student List first.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency, using the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which is waived for ethnic-minority lists. Sixteen electoral lists are registered.

Vučić resigned as President on September 27, 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as candidate for Prime Minister. Ana Brnabić became acting president. The list's first three candidates are Vučić, Miloš Vučević and Ana Brnabić.
Vučić called early parliamentary elections for October 25, 2026, and the Assembly was dissolved on September 9. The elections were originally due by December 2027.

Registered lists include United Serbia (SNS-led, submitted Sept 12; ballot number 1), SPS-led 'Factor of Stability' (Sept 12), 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (Sept 14; ballot number 3) and the opposition coalition European Serbia (SSP–Serbia Centre–Solidarity, Sept 19). Some opposition parties withdrew to back the Student List.

CRTA's campaign monitoring reports that the Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, has had no live appearances on national TV since the list was declared on September 15. Over the same period Vučić made 17 appearances, in which he portrayed the Student List as 'anti-Serbian' and acting on 'orders from abroad'. Vučić has called CRTA's polls propaganda, and CRTA says he is trying to discredit it as an election observer.

recent_facts.fact: UNVERIFIED (from memory): an SNS-led list won the most seats in all 6 Serbian parliamentary elections since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023). In 2023 it won 129 of 250 seats with about 46.8% of the vote.

Election day is October 25, 2026, which is also the day the question closes. RIK (Republic Electoral Commission) publishes preliminary and final results, and new polls are expected in early-to-mid October.
Older context: a CRTA poll from September 13–27, 2025 had the student list at 44% and Vučić's bloc at 32%. In the same poll, 58% supported the anti-government protests and 39% opposed them.

market.question: Will there be more than 30 transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026? (Above 30)
market.rules:
If the number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 30 from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The total is calculated by summing daily counts from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

recent_facts.fact: As of 2026-10-05, the IMF PortWatch 7-day average for the Strait of Hormuz was about 3 commercial ships per day. That is roughly 21 transits a week, against a pre-crisis norm of about 85 a day. The latest daily figure shown is 1 transit on 2026-09-27.
The Oct 4 brief says IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, the most recent published day, against a baseline of 85 a day. It gives no PortWatch daily counts for Sep 28–Oct 4 yet.

IMF PortWatch publishes weekly, usually on Tuesday, with about a two-day lag. Its counts come from AIS signals, so ships that go dark or are jammed are missed and its counts run lower than other trackers.

Straits.live reported 8 vessels transited on October 1, against a baseline of about 88 a day, and said 4 of the 8 had AIS transponders switched off. This is not a PortWatch figure, and PortWatch, which relies on AIS, would likely miss the dark ships.

A tracker summary cites PortWatch-based AIS-visible traffic averaging 6.1 ships a day over a recent week (day 219 of the crisis), or 43 crossings: 16 tankers, 27 cargo ships and no LNG/LPG carriers. The exact week covered is unclear.
PortWatch recorded a single transit on 2026-09-20. Reuters commodity-vessel counts, which use a different method, were 7 on Sep 22 and 10 on Sep 23, with a 10-day moving average of about 17.

recent_facts.source: Search summary (likely Lloyd's List transit monitor, not PortWatch)
recent_facts.fact: A non-PortWatch tracker reported 114 transits for Sep 21–27 and 137 for Sep 14–20, which counts much higher than PortWatch's roughly 3 a day. I couldn't confirm which provider produced this figure, so treat it as unverified.
Iranian media (Fars) claimed the IRGC targeted seven tankers in the strait over five days. As of Oct 4, 247 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Hormuz area.

At least six vessels were struck in the strait in the week before Oct 4, including a Kuwait-flagged tanker on Oct 1. Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd have suspended transits, and six P&I clubs have withdrawn cover.
Iran said in October that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until its demands are met.
On Sep 23, CENTCOM said 115 commercial vessels had been redirected under the US blockade, which resumed on July 14. US–Iran talks on a phased arrangement had not settled the two sides' differences.
PortWatch daily data for Sep 28–Oct 4 should appear in the weekly update, usually on Tuesday (Oct 6). The question closes 2026-10-06 13:00 UTC.

market.question: Will the rate of core CPI inflation be above 2.4% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 2.4%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy increases by more than 2.4% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS reported that CPI-U all items less food and energy rose 2.4% (not seasonally adjusted) in the 12 months ending August 2026, down from 2.5% in July. Usinflationcalculator called it the lowest 12-month core rate since March 2021.

recent_facts.source: Search-result summary of August 2026 CPI coverage (original page not identified)
recent_facts.fact: A search summary said unrounded core CPI rose about 2.45% year over year in August 2026, which BLS rounded to 2.4%. This could not be checked directly: the page returned 403, and the summary may have drawn on other results. Treat it as unverified.
Seasonally adjusted month-over-month core CPI in 2026: Feb +0.2%, Mar +0.2%, Apr +0.4%, May +0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul +0.2%, Aug +0.3%. August came in one-tenth above most estimates.

The month leaving the 12-month window is September 2025. In that month the core index rose 0.2% seasonally adjusted and 3.0% over 12 months. The 12-month change for September 2026 will roughly hold at the August level if the September 2026 core monthly gain is close to September 2025's gain, and move up or down if it is larger or smaller.
Shelter, the largest core component, rose 0.3% in August 2026 after two straight monthly gains of 0.1%. It was up 3.0% year over year.

recent_facts.source: Search-result summary of August 2026 CPI coverage (citing Advisor Perspectives / Yahoo Finance)
recent_facts.fact: Headline CPI rose 0.4% in August 2026 and 3.4% year over year, driven by higher gasoline prices. That energy surge is excluded from the core measure that decides this question.
BLS is scheduled to release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET. The question closes at 12:25 UTC that day, just before the release.

The question resolves on the one-decimal, not seasonally adjusted 12-month percent change in CPI-U all items less food and energy published by BLS. A reading of exactly 2.4% resolves No; 2.5% or higher resolves Yes.

recent_facts.fact: No. 2 Georgia (5-0, 3-0 SEC) plays No. 6 Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC) on Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC. The game is at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, so Alabama is the true home team. Both markets resolve on the official final result. College football has overtime, so the game cannot end in a tie.

Georgia is 2-14 in games played in Tuscaloosa. Its last win there was 26-23 in overtime on Sept 22, 2007, which SI/Hot Augusta also report. Alabama won the last two Tuscaloosa meetings: 41-24 in 2020 and 41-34 in 2024.

Alabama leads the all-time series 45-27-4. Alabama won 7 of the last 10 meetings and Georgia won 3. The two most recent: Alabama won 24-21 in Athens on Sept 27, 2025, and Georgia won 28-7 in the SEC Championship in Atlanta on Dec 6, 2025. This is a small sample covering different venues and coaching eras.

Alabama is 5-0 after beating Mississippi State 56-23 on the road on Oct 3. Its earlier results: 48-10 vs East Carolina, 45-17 at Kentucky, 50-36 vs Florida State and 49-18 vs South Carolina. That is 248 points scored and 104 allowed.

Georgia is 5-0: 63-3 vs Tennessee State (FCS), 70-20 vs Western Kentucky, 45-17 at Arkansas, 41-13 vs Oklahoma and 38-14 vs Vanderbilt. That is 257 points scored and 67 allowed. Wikipedia lists Alabama as Georgia's first ranked opponent of the season.

In the 38-14 win over Vanderbilt, Georgia QB Gunner Stockton went 25 of 32 for a season-high 295 yards and 3 TDs. Georgia ran for 176 yards on 34 carries and held Vanderbilt to 293 total yards, 61 of them in the second half. Vanderbilt was playing its backup QB.
Gunner Stockton, a fifth-year player, has started all five Georgia games. Wikipedia reports no significant Georgia injuries through Week 5.

Before the Mississippi State game, Kalen DeBoer said right tackle Jayvin James was questionable with a lower-extremity injury from the South Carolina game. He also said William Sanders had an upper-body injury and was expected to play. Linebackers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu were out, with Umeozulu out longer. Reports describe Alabama's offensive line as banged up. No status update for Georgia week was found.
President Trump announced he will attend the game in Tuscaloosa. It is the third straight year the two teams meet in the regular season.

market.question: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Nov 1, 2026? (Before Nov 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

market.question: Will BTC trimmed mean be above $90000.00 by 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026? (Above $90,000.00)
market.rules:
If the price of BTC after issuance and through 11:59 PM ET on Oct 31, 2026 is ever above $
90000.00, then the market resolves to Yes.
At each minute throughout the market duration, a settlement value is calculated using every minute-by-minute CF BRTI price for BTC. recent_facts.fact: As of 2026-10-05, the IMF PortWatch 7-day average for the Strait of Hormuz was about 3 commercial ships per day. That is roughly 21 transits a week, against a pre-crisis norm of about 85 a day. The latest daily figure shown is 1 transit on 2026-09-27.
The Oct 4 brief says IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, the most recent published day, against a baseline of 85 a day. It gives no PortWatch daily counts for Sep 28–Oct 4 yet.

IMF PortWatch publishes weekly, usually on Tuesday, with about a two-day lag. Its counts come from AIS signals, so ships that go dark or are jammed are missed and its counts run lower than other trackers.

Straits.live reported 8 vessels transited on October 1, against a baseline of about 88 a day, and said 4 of the 8 had AIS transponders switched off. This is not a PortWatch figure, and PortWatch, which relies on AIS, would likely miss the dark ships.

A tracker summary cites PortWatch-based AIS-visible traffic averaging 6.1 ships a day over a recent week (day 219 of the crisis), or 43 crossings: 16 tankers, 27 cargo ships and no LNG/LPG carriers. The exact week covered is unclear.
PortWatch recorded a single transit on 2026-09-20. Reuters commodity-vessel counts, which use a different method, were 7 on Sep 22 and 10 on Sep 23, with a 10-day moving average of about 17.

recent_facts.source: Search summary (likely Lloyd's List transit monitor, not PortWatch)

Iran said in October that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until its demands are met.
On Sep 23, CENTCOM said 115 commercial vessels had been redirected under the US blockade, which resumed on July 14. US–Iran talks on a phased arrangement had not settled the two sides' differences.
PortWatch daily data for Sep 28–Oct 4 should appear in the weekly update, usually on Tuesday (Oct 6). The question closes 2026-10-06 13:00 UTC.

market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Channel 13 poll, fielded Sept 30 (n=1,103, MoE 2.5%): Netanyahu bloc 54 seats (Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 8, UTJ 8, Shas 7, Religious Zionism 7). Opposition Jewish bloc 52 (Yashar 21, Together 11, Democrats 11, Yisrael Beiteinu 9). Arab parties 14. Neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority.
Maariv poll: Netanyahu bloc 51 seats, opposition 53, Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 9. The Netanyahu bloc gained 2 seats from Maariv's previous poll and neither camp reaches 61.

Late-September polls disagree on Netanyahu's bloc total. Channel 14: 63 (Likud 32). i24NEWS: 60 (Likud 27). Zman Yisrael: 53. Channel 13: 51. N12: 50. Maariv: 49. Yashar is at 22-23 in most of them. The Reservists party is placed in different blocs by different pollsters, which moves bloc totals by several seats.

The election is set for October 27, 2026, after the Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026 at the end of its full term. The threshold is 3.25% and 61 of 120 seats are needed for a majority. Netanyahu is the incumbent PM and Likud's candidate, with New Hope merged into Likud.

The question resolves only on a PM formally sworn in after the 2026 election; a caretaker PM does not count. If Netanyahu stays on as caretaker during coalition talks, that is not a swearing-in. If nobody is sworn in by Dec 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The question closes Oct 28, 2026, one day after the vote.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: after the Nov 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu's government was sworn in on Dec 29, 2022, about 58 days later. Israeli government formation usually takes weeks to months, so no swearing-in would be expected by the Oct 28 close.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: of the 6 Knesset elections from 2015 to 2022, the PM sworn in directly after the vote was Netanyahu after 2015, 2020 and 2022, and Bennett after 2021. The April 2019 and Sept 2019 elections produced no government and led to repeat elections.

On Sept 23 the Central Elections Committee disqualified Ra'am and the Joint List. The Supreme Court overturned that on Oct 2, and on Oct 4 it rejected further disqualification appeals. Petitions against Otzma Yehudit were rejected on Sept 24.

Bennett said he is willing to give up the premiership in a post-Netanyahu government. The opposition Jewish parties (Yashar, Together, Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu) have said they won't form a coalition that includes Arab parties. Lieberman has not endorsed any PM candidate.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: On October 2–3, Trump said the Iran war would end "very soon" and "probably right after the midterms" (November 3). The White House said the US is "winning" its economic campaign and that Iranian oil exports have stopped completely because of the blockade.

Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first month at zero since the war began in February, and the US blockade was still in force.
Trump is sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Iranian inflation is near 90%, and diplomacy is described as deadlocked.

Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire. Under that proposal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart talks, and its conditions included lifting the US port blockade, releasing frozen funds and waiving oil sanctions. Trump said "that deal would not be acceptable."

Indirect talks are continuing through Qatari mediators. Foreign Minister Araghchi expected a formal US response by about September 29. A US official called the talks "positive and constructive" but said there would be no deal unless the nuclear issues are addressed. Trump said "I offered them NOTHING" in reply to reports of possible sanctions relief.
Reports say Trump told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 midterm elections if negotiations fail.

On October 4, Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the strait will stay closed until Iran's conditions are met. The report says Tehran wants a deal before the November 3 election, while Trump talks of ending the war after it.
Axios reported that envoys Witkoff and Kushner and Vice President Vance still believed diplomacy was worth pursuing, while Trump appeared much more skeptical.

After talks around the UN General Assembly, Trump called the discussions "very good" but demanded better terms than Iran had offered. Treasury added sanctions on Iranian railway and automotive firms on October 1.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran) / NPR
recent_facts.fact: The first blockade phase began on April 13, 2026. It ended after a deal was announced on June 14 and signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18, about 66 days in. Removal came only as part of a signed ceasefire agreement that started a 60-day negotiation period.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran)
recent_facts.fact: Trump announced on July 13 that the blockade would be reinstated, and it resumed on July 14–15. CENTCOM reported 55 vessels redirected by August 11 and more than 100 by September 12. The page records no announcement about ending the blockade from August through early October.

The last time the blockade was lifted, the official announcement came from CENTCOM after a signed US–Iran memorandum. That is the kind of official-channel, general lifting the resolution rules require; an exemption for a specific vessel or cargo would not count.

The key upcoming date is the US midterm election on November 3, 2026, which falls after both closing dates (October 15 and October 31). No formal US–Iran negotiating round had been publicly scheduled as of October 4.

market.question: Will England win on 2026-10-06?

In the upcoming game, scheduled for October 6, 2026
If England wins, this market will resolve to "Yes".
Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".
If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed.
If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve "No".
This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 31?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The East-West pipeline restarted on September 22, 2026 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd. The report rests on Reuters sources and does not cite any announcement from the Saudi government, the Ministry of Energy or SPA.

Saudi Aramco is reported to be pumping close to 6 million bpd through the 7 million bpd East-West pipeline, more than 80% of capacity, after the September 22 restart. The report notes that Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not respond to requests for comment, so no official confirmation is cited. Date approximate (early October).

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on September 10–11. The attacks hit the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing fires, some damage and injuries.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the Saudi pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. This is a US official speaking, not the Saudi government.

The 7 million bpd pipeline carries crude to Red Sea export terminals and has been Saudi Arabia's main way around Hormuz during the Iran war. Brent rose more than 3% to $108 after the shutdown. Later reports said Yanbu loadings had picked up, a sign the pipeline was running again.

recent_facts.source: Saudi Press Agency / Al Jazeera / Fortune
recent_facts.fact: Precedent: after the earlier 2026 attacks cut East-West throughput by about 700,000 bpd, the Ministry of Energy issued an SPA statement on April 12, 2026 saying full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored, along with 300,000 bpd at Manifa. That was an official, public restoration announcement within days of the damage.

SPA headline: 'Ministry of Energy: Energy Facilities and East–West Pipeline Affected by the Attacks Have Recovered and Restored Operational Capacity'. Coverage dates this statement to April 12, 2026, which is before the September shutdown and outside the market window. The page shows no date, so the date is inferred from news coverage. One search summary attributed a similar ministry statement to September 29, 2026, but this could not be confirmed and is probably confused with the April statement.

The question closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Only an official Saudi government statement that the pipeline is operating now counts, and partial capacity is enough. Reports from Reuters, Bloomberg or Kpler sources, and statements about future resumption, do not count.

market.question: Will Likud win 30-34 seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the number of seats won by the Likud party in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the Likud party contests this election as part of a joint candidate list with one or more parties, all seats won by the joint candidate list will be counted. If the Likud party merges with another party prior to the election, all seats won by the resultant merged party, or any joint candidate list through which it contests the election, will be counted.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by October 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest range bracket.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the Likud party in this election.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $80 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will Bitcoin be above $100000 by November 1, 2026 at 12:00AM ET? (Before November 2026)
market.rules:
If the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $100000.00 starting Jul 21, 2026 and before Nov 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States House of Representatives elections)
recent_facts.fact: The current House has 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats and 1 independent. All 435 seats are up for election on November 3, 2026, and a majority takes 218 seats.

Other generic-ballot aggregates show Democrats ahead by about 7 to 9 points in early October 2026. One average has Democrats at 50.8% and Republicans at 43.1%, and Democratic support ranges from 48.8% to 52.0% across pollsters. Decision Desk HQ's average shows a Democratic lead of about 6 points.

In October 2026, Trump's approval averages 37.3% approve and 60.3% disapprove (net -23.0), with individual trackers ranging from 34% to 39% approve. His approval among independents is 34%, below the 36% seen before Democrats gained 41 seats in 2018.
One month before the midterms, Trump's approval is underwater in 39 states and in every major battleground state.

The president's party has lost House seats in 18 of the 20 midterms since 1946, with an average loss of about 25 to 26 seats. The two exceptions were 1998 (Democrats +5) and 2002 (Republicans +8). The publication date shown is approximate.

When the president's approval was below 50%, his party lost an average of 37 House seats in midterms, compared with an average of 14 when approval was above 50%. This covers data through 2014 only; the publication date shown is approximate.

Mid-decade redistricting moved seats in both directions: Texas about +5 for Republicans, California about +5 for Democrats, Missouri +1 R, North Carolina +1 R and Ohio +2 R. Accounts put the overall net Republican gain from redistricting at about 5 to 8 seats.

In the Louisiana (Callais) case, the Supreme Court struck down Louisiana's map as a racial gerrymander, weakening the Voting Rights Act. Afterward, Louisiana, Alabama, Florida and Tennessee enacted new maps.
Louisiana approved a new map that eliminates one majority-Black district, which would change the delegation from 4R-2D to 5R-1D. The date shown is approximate.

On September 25, 2026, the Cook Political Report moved 15 House races toward Democrats. AZ-1 and NJ-7 went from Toss-up to Lean Democrat, and three seats, including TX-15 (De La Cruz), went from Likely Republican to Toss-up. Cook now rates 23 races as Toss-ups: 17 held by Republicans and 5 by Democrats.

recent_facts.fact: A record 61 representatives are retiring (37 Republicans and 26 Democrats), the second-highest number after 1992. At least 11 Democratic-held districts were won by Trump.

recent_facts.fact: Election day is November 3, 2026, and both questions close on 2026-11-04 at 04:59 UTC. Some states, such as Louisiana and Georgia, may hold runoffs later, and the rules count runoff results.

facts_dropped.fact: As of October 2, 2026, Democrats lead the generic congressional ballot by 9.0 points (9.6 with a likely-voter adjustment). Their lead was 6.7 points at the start of September.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In 270toWin's average of the 5 most recent general-election polls, Democrat James Talarico has 49.6% and Republican Ken Paxton has 45.6%. Talarico leads in all 10 polls the site lists from Sept. 10 to Oct. 3, 2026, by between 1 and 6 points.

A Siena College poll released Oct. 3, 2026 (615 likely voters, ±4.5%) has Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 45%. Siena's earlier poll, released Sept. 17 (614 likely voters), had Talarico 49% to Paxton 43%.
A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters (±3%) has Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, inside the margin of error. Talarico's favorability is 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable. Paxton's is 40% to 58%.

Pulse Decision Science, a conservative polling firm, surveyed 800 likely voters Sept. 24–27 and found Paxton at 48% and Talarico at 45%. It was the first poll in weeks to show Paxton ahead. Undecided voters fell from 11% in May to 4%.
A Marist poll of 1,139 Texas registered voters (Sept. 17–20, ±4.4%) has Talarico at 50% and Paxton at 44%. Talarico gets 55% among independents.

Other recent polls: Texas Public Opinion Research, Talarico 49% to Paxton 44%; Texas Southern University, 47% to 46%; Trafalgar, 46% to 45%; Emerson, 47% to 46%; Mason-Dixon, 46% to 43%; InsiderAdvantage, 47% to 46%.
A new Texas political action committee spent $131 million in 17 days to boost Paxton's Senate campaign.
Talarico and Paxton launched competing ads. Talarico's ad accuses Paxton of using AI-generated videos to lie about his record.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026. The questions close Nov. 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC, which is election night.

The last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988, so Republicans have won every Texas Senate election since. Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office since 1994.

Texas polls understated the Democrat in 2018, were close in 2022, and understated the Republican Senate margin in 2020 and 2024. In 2024, final averages had Cruz ahead by about 4 points and Emerson's final poll had him up 48–47, but he won by 8.5.

Recent Texas Senate margins, recalled from memory and not checked against a source: Cruz beat O'Rourke by about 2.6 points in 2018, Cornyn won by about 9.6 in 2020, and Cruz beat Allred by about 8.5 in 2024.

The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification. Runoffs count. Independents do not count as either party's nominee.

facts_dropped.fact: Paxton won the May 26 Republican runoff with about 64% to incumbent Sen. John Cornyn's roughly 35%, after Trump endorsed Paxton. Cornyn is the first sitting Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's nomination. Talarico won the Democratic nomination on March 3 with 52.4% over Rep. Jasmine Crockett.

market.question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: According to IMF PortWatch, Bab el-Mandeb traffic averaged 28 vessels/day in August 2026, the lowest monthly level in the recent series. A 3-day sample to about 11 September averaged about 26/day (79 vessels), and the 7-day moving average was 24/day on 29 July.

A late-September update said IMF PortWatch recorded a single transit for 20 September, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85/day. It did not say whether this was a preliminary or lagged figure, and it gave no 7-day average. Neither the figure nor which strait it refers to has been checked against PortWatch.

recent_facts.source: Search summary of late-September shipping reports (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Reports summarized in search results said IMF PortWatch AIS data for Bab el-Mandeb in mid-to-late September 2026 showed daily volumes in the low-to-mid 20s, with about 22 vessels on recent days. This has not been checked against the PortWatch page itself.

Lloyd's List Intelligence's own Red Sea Transit Monitor counted 290 preliminary Bab el-Mandeb transits for 21–27 September 2026 (264 the week before), a 4-week weekly average of 280, against 316 in June and 257 in January. This counting method differs from PortWatch's and gives higher numbers.
In early to mid September 2026, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast down to the Bab el-Mandeb, including the port of Mocha. Other reports say they also took Perim Island and the Hanish Islands.
Windward reported that Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from 35 daily transits before the Houthi advance to 25 after. Traffic then recovered, reaching 45 transits on one Sunday in mid-September.

The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in September 2026 and said Saudi shipping using the strait would be targeted. There have been 12 Houthi attacks or attempted attacks on commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea since July 2026.
The Houthis told the EU in a letter that they would not target European ships in the Red Sea and that their activity would not affect navigation through Bab el-Mandeb.

On 4 October 2026, the Saudi-led coalition pledged support for a Yemeni government offensive against the Houthis. ABC News reported the same day that the Houthis targeted a Saudi oil facility as hostilities escalated.

The Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia, imposed on 20 July 2026, reduced crude exports through the Yanbu terminals. The Saudi pipeline has resumed at reduced rates, and some operators are increasingly sending ships back through the Red Sea.
A Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb on 11 August 2026 killed four to six crew. The PortWatch monthly average stayed at 28/day for August.

recent_facts.source: Anadolu Agency (citing IMF PortWatch / World Bank)
recent_facts.fact: PortWatch daily averages: about 71/day from January 2022 to October 2023; 43/day from 17 November 2023 to 19 February 2024; about 33.5/day in 2025; 34–37/day in January–July 2026; 28/day in August 2026. None of the figures found here comes close to a 7-day average of 10 or below, including through the 2024–2025 Houthi campaign. This is not a full check of PortWatch's daily series.

The question resolves Yes if PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of Bab el-Mandeb transit calls of 10 or below for any date through 31 October 2026. PortWatch counts AIS-visible transits, so ships with AIS off are not counted. Revisions are considered only until the 31 October data is published.
PortWatch daily data is published with a lag. Data for dates up to 31 October must appear within 14 days after that date, and the question closes on 1 November 2026 (03:59 UTC).

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Maine Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Maine U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A CBS News poll of 1,144 Maine registered voters, fielded Sept 23–Oct 1, 2026 (MOE ±4.7), shows Republican Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson tied. 10% of voters are undecided, and 10% say they could still change their minds.
A NYT/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll has Collins at 49% and Jackson at 46%, with a margin of error of about ±4.9. Newsweek reported this as Collins's first lead over Jackson in an independent poll.

A UNH Survey Center poll released 9/24/2026 has Jackson at 51% and Collins at 47%, which UNH calls a statistical tie, largely unchanged since July. Independents split 49% Jackson, 47% Collins. Collins's favorability among likely voters is 37% favorable, 51% unfavorable.

A Wedgewood poll dated Oct 1 shows Jackson 52%, Collins 48%. The Pollsmax polling average has Jackson ahead 49.5% to 46.5%. These figures come from a search-result summary, not a full read of the page.

Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary but withdrew on July 10 after a sexual assault allegation, which he denies. On July 25 a Democratic convention in Bangor nominated former state Senate president Troy Jackson, who beat Saundra Pelletier 566 votes to 5.
Jackson is the first replacement U.S. Senate nominee in Maine since 1918. He is now the Democratic nominee for resolution purposes, and Collins is the Republican nominee.

Maine's general election uses ranked-choice voting, so if no one wins a first-round majority, the result can depend on later-round tabulation. The race resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call it, or otherwise on official certification.
The general election is on November 3, 2026, and the question closes on November 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC.
