market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: The East-West pipeline restarted on September 22, 2026 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million bpd. The report rests on Reuters sources and does not cite any announcement from the Saudi government, the Ministry of Energy or SPA.

Saudi Aramco is reported to be pumping close to 6 million bpd through the 7 million bpd East-West pipeline, more than 80% of capacity, after the September 22 restart. The report notes that Aramco and the Saudi energy ministry did not respond to requests for comment, so no official confirmation is cited. Date approximate (early October).

The Ministry of Energy said the East–West pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone attacks launched from Iraq on September 10–11. The attacks hit the Riyadh and Medina regions, causing fires, some damage and injuries.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the Saudi pipeline closure would be a brief interruption lasting days. This is a US official speaking, not the Saudi government.

The 7 million bpd pipeline carries crude to Red Sea export terminals and has been Saudi Arabia's main way around Hormuz during the Iran war. Brent rose more than 3% to $108 after the shutdown. Later reports said Yanbu loadings had picked up, a sign the pipeline was running again.

recent_facts.source: Saudi Press Agency / Al Jazeera / Fortune
recent_facts.fact: Precedent: after the earlier 2026 attacks cut East-West throughput by about 700,000 bpd, the Ministry of Energy issued an SPA statement on April 12, 2026 saying full pumping capacity of about 7 million bpd had been restored, along with 300,000 bpd at Manifa. market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a ceasefire agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify. Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement. Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g. restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

All listed countries/parties must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for a Yes resolution. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a ceasefire agreement will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where a potentially qualifying announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a ceasefire agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries/parties or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 7 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the seventh calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, the announcements will be judged based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia and Houthi leadership; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Saudi Aramco cut its November Arab Light price to Asia to $5 below the regional benchmark as Middle Eastern flows normalize. Saudi-backed forces in Yemen launched operations against Houthi areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and OPEC+ kept quotas unchanged.

market.rules:

recent_facts.fact: The Brewers beat the Padres 4-3 in NLDS Game 2 on a two-run walk-off single by Jackson Chourio in the ninth, after three walks off Padres closer Mason Miller. Milwaukee leads the best-of-five NLDS 2-0 and needs one more win to advance.

The Braves beat the defending champion Dodgers 3-2 in NLDS Game 2, tying the best-of-five series 1-1. Atlanta lost Game 1 5-3 in a bullpen game. A CBS Sports summary gave the Game 2 score as 3-1, but its own text says the Braves allowed two runs, which fits 3-2.

NLDS Game 3 between the Dodgers and Braves is Tuesday, Oct. 6, at 6 p.m. ET at Truist Park. Chris Sale (2.16 ERA, third-best in MLB) starts on extra rest against Yoshinobu Yamamoto, the 2025 World Series MVP.

Brewers-Padres NLDS Game 3 is Tuesday, Oct. 6, at 9:30 p.m. ET at Petco Park, Dustin May against Nick Pivetta. May had a 1.23 ERA with 22 strikeouts in 22 innings over three starts against San Diego this season. Pivetta has a 1.45 ERA over his last four starts after missing nearly five months with a flexor tendon injury.
NLDS Game 3 is Oct. 6, Game 4 (if needed) is Oct. 7 and Game 5 (if needed) is Oct. 9. The NL bracket pairs Dodgers-Braves and Brewers-Padres, and the two winners meet in the NLCS.

The League Championship Series run Oct. 11–20 and the best-of-seven World Series runs Oct. 23–31, with a possible Game 7 on Oct. 31. The champion would be decided before the questions close on Oct. 31 at 23:55 UTC.
The Braves reached the NLDS by beating the Phillies 2-1 in the NL Wild Card Series, winning the deciding Game 3 6-2.

In Game 2, Atlanta used reliever Ray Kerr as an opener; he got eight outs without allowing a run. 21-year-old Didier Fuentes allowed only a solo homer over four innings. The Dodgers managed just two solo homers, by Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman.
In the AL Division Series, the Rays face the Yankees and the White Sox face the Guardians. The Rays and White Sox each led their series 1-0 after Game 1; ALDS Game 2 is Oct. 5.

market.rules:

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Channel 13 poll, fielded Sept 30 (n=1,103, MoE 2.5%): Netanyahu bloc 54 seats (Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 8, UTJ 8, Shas 7, Religious Zionism 7). Opposition Jewish bloc 52 (Yashar 21, Together 11, Democrats 11, Yisrael Beiteinu 9). Arab parties 14. Neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority.
Maariv poll: Netanyahu bloc 51 seats, opposition 53, Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 9. The Netanyahu bloc gained 2 seats from Maariv's previous poll and neither camp reaches 61.

Late-September polls disagree on Netanyahu's bloc total. Channel 14: 63 (Likud 32). i24NEWS: 60 (Likud 27). Zman Yisrael: 53. Channel 13: 51. N12: 50. Maariv: 49. Yashar is at 22-23 in most of them. The Reservists party is placed in different blocs by different pollsters, which moves bloc totals by several seats.

The election is set for October 27, 2026, after the Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026 at the end of its full term. The threshold is 3.25% and 61 of 120 seats are needed for a majority. Netanyahu is the incumbent PM and Likud's candidate, with New Hope merged into Likud.

The question resolves only on a PM formally sworn in after the 2026 election; a caretaker PM does not count. If Netanyahu stays on as caretaker during coalition talks, that is not a swearing-in. If nobody is sworn in by Dec 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The question closes Oct 28, 2026, one day after the vote.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: after the Nov 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu's government was sworn in on Dec 29, 2022, about 58 days later. Israeli government formation usually takes weeks to months, so no swearing-in would be expected by the Oct 28 close.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: of the 6 Knesset elections from 2015 to 2022, the PM sworn in directly after the vote was Netanyahu after 2015, 2020 and 2022, and Bennett after 2021. The April 2019 and Sept 2019 elections produced no government and led to repeat elections.

On Sept 23 the Central Elections Committee disqualified Ra'am and the Joint List. The Supreme Court overturned that on Oct 2, and on Oct 4 it rejected further disqualification appeals. Petitions against Otzma Yehudit were rejected on Sept 24.

Bennett said he is willing to give up the premiership in a post-Netanyahu government. The opposition Jewish parties (Yashar, Together, Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu) have said they won't form a coalition that includes Arab parties. Lieberman has not endorsed any PM candidate.
Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg ordered Netanyahu to remove campaign videos that made unauthorized use of the IDF and public resources.

Netanyahu is under pressure over a Wall Street Journal report that Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel warned him by phone days before the Oct 7, 2023 attack. On Oct 3, Eisenkot connected Netanyahu's rejection of a state inquiry to a flydubai near-disaster.

Election day is Oct 27, 2026. After that the President consults with parties and assigns a candidate to form a government, and the new government must win a Knesset vote and be sworn in. Under the question's rules, this has to happen by Dec 31, 2027.

recent_facts.fact: An early parliamentary election for all 250 National Assembly seats is set for 25 October 2026, after Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 September. Seats are allocated by closed-list PR with d'Hondt and a 3% threshold, which is waived for minority parties. A majority is 126 seats.

Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist and medical professor born in 1970, heads the ballot for the 'Student List – Students Are Winning' in the 2026 election. Reporting describes him as the Student List's lead candidate for prime minister.
Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister. He heads SNS's 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list.

Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister on 3 October at Belgrade Arena and promised a 'comprehensive' victory. Al Jazeera reports that if SNS wins a majority, parliament would elect Vučić as PM. It describes the Student List as the main challenger.
A Faktor Plus poll had Vučić's United Serbia at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%. That was a 5.6-point gain for the Student List.
An NSPM poll presented by Vukadinović had the Student List at 44.4% and United Serbia at 41.7%. The exact publication date is approximate: late September or early October 2026.
A CRTA survey found 44% of respondents backing the Student List and 32% backing Vučić's bloc. The publication date is approximate: September 2026.
Speaking from New York, Vučić was reported as saying the Student List leads and is 'hard to catch'.
Another poll had the Student List at 39.6% and SNS at 37.5%. Wikipedia sums up recent polling as a tightened race in which results vary by pollster.

Other lists include European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš), Authentic Right (Miloš Jovanović) and the SPS-led Factor of Stability (Ivica Dačić). SSP said it would cooperate with the Student List. PSG dropped out of the race to back the Student List.
Election day is 25 October 2026, the same day this question closes. A PM can only be elected later, after the new Assembly holds its constitutive session.

market.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

recent_facts.fact: Faktor Plus poll (Sept 16–20, 2026, 986 respondents) has 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' at 48.6% (+1.4 on the month) and the Student List at 37.1% (+5.6). SPS polled 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8% and Nestorović's list 1.2%. Expected turnout was about 62%, and 16% were undecided.

An NSPM (Nova srpska politička misao) poll from the first ten days of September 2026, published in Vreme on October 1, has the Student List at 44.3% and Vučić's list at 41.7%. The analyst Vukadinović notes that the fieldwork came before the election was called, before some parties withdrew to back the Student List, and before Nestorović's list was eliminated.

Earlier Faktor Plus polls had SNS well ahead: 46.4% vs 28.7% in April, 47.1% vs 30.7% in June, and 47.2% vs 31.5% in early September 2026 (n=1,200). Faktor Plus has had SNS first in every poll, while CRTA and NSPM have had the Student List first.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency, using the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which is waived for ethnic-minority lists. Sixteen electoral lists are registered.

Vučić resigned as President on September 27, 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as candidate for Prime Minister. Ana Brnabić became acting president. The list's first three candidates are Vučić, Miloš Vučević and Ana Brnabić.
Vučić called early parliamentary elections for October 25, 2026, and the Assembly was dissolved on September 9. The elections were originally due by December 2027.

Registered lists include United Serbia (SNS-led, submitted Sept 12; ballot number 1), SPS-led 'Factor of Stability' (Sept 12), 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (Sept 14; ballot number 3) and the opposition coalition European Serbia (SSP–Serbia Centre–Solidarity, Sept 19). Some opposition parties withdrew to back the Student List.

CRTA's campaign monitoring reports that the Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, has had no live appearances on national TV since the list was declared on September 15. Over the same period Vučić made 17 appearances, in which he portrayed the Student List as 'anti-Serbian' and acting on 'orders from abroad'. Vučić has called CRTA's polls propaganda, and CRTA says he is trying to discredit it as an election observer.

market.question: Israel accuses Iran/proxies of plane stabbing incident by Oct 31?
market.rules:
On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: On Sept. 22, 2026, Premier David Eby called a snap B.C. general election for Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, about two years early. He framed it around U.S. trade threats. The vote comes one week after the Oct. 17 municipal elections and is estimated to cost $83–84 million.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. market.question: Will Saudi airspace be closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Saudi Arabian Airspace (The Jeddah Flight Information Region (FIR)/OEJD) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before market creation; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before market creation, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Saudi Arabian government, including the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), and Saudi Air Navigation Services (SANS), and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Only the result after 90 minutes plus stoppage time counts. A draw or a Canada win resolves No, and it is a friendly, so there is no extra time.

The USMNT host Canada in a friendly on October 6, 2026 at 8pm ET at Allianz Field in St. Paul, Minnesota. It is a US home venue, not a neutral ground, and it is the last match of the window before the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals in November.

The USMNT have won all three friendlies since the World Cup: 4-1 over Peru (Sept 26), 4-2 over Chile (Sept 29) and 3-0 over Mexico (Oct 3). That is 11-3 on aggregate. Their World Cup ended with a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the Round of 16 on July 6.

Canada have won both matches this window, 1-0 over Chile and 2-0 over Peru in Montreal on Oct 3. Against Peru they outshot their opponent 17-4, with xG of 1.94 to 0.23 and Jacob Shaffelburg scoring twice.
U.S. Soccer gives the all-time record as USA 17 wins, 12 losses and 13 draws against Canada. A 2025 U.S. Soccer preview cited elsewhere gives 20-14-11, so the sources disagree (unverified).

Canada won the last two meetings, both 2-1: a friendly in Kansas City on Sept 7, 2024 and the Nations League third-place match on March 23, 2025. The two teams have not played each other in 2026. This is a small sample.
The 2-1 loss in Kansas City in September 2024 was the first US home defeat to Canada in 67 years. Canada's previous win on US soil was 3-2 in St. Louis in 1957.

Canada's listed absences include Alphonso Davies, Alistair Johnston, Ismaël Koné, Moïse Bombito, Jonathan Osorio, Kamal Miller, Derek Cornelius, Ali Ahmed, Jayden Nelson and Maxime Crépeau. Tajon Buchanan and Cyle Larin left camp injured.

Pochettino started a very experienced team against Mexico, apart from teenagers Julian Hall and Cavan Sullivan, who both scored. He is reported to be planning more rotation against Canada, with Sergino Dest, George Campbell and Neil Pierre in line for minutes in defense.

At the 2026 World Cup, Canada drew 1-1 with Bosnia and Herzegovina, beat Qatar 6-0 and lost 2-1 to Switzerland, finishing second in Group D. They then beat South Africa 1-0 and were knocked out by Morocco. Earlier in 2026 they drew with Iceland, Tunisia and Ireland and beat Uzbekistan 2-0.

US results in 2026 before the World Cup were mixed: they lost 5-2 to Belgium and 2-0 to Portugal, beat Senegal 3-2 and lost 2-1 to Germany. At the World Cup they went 3 wins and 2 losses (4-1 Paraguay, 2-0 Australia, 2-3 Türkiye, 2-0 Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1-4 Belgium).

AAA's weekly national average gasoline price rose through September 2026: $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and $4.48 on Sept 24. AAA called Sept 24 the highest ever for that time of year. On Sept 17 it was more than $1 above a year earlier.

AAA said the September 2026 monthly average was a record for the month at $4.33, 50 cents above the previous September record. It blamed Strait of Hormuz volatility and high crude prices. By October 1 the average had dropped nearly 7 cents to $4.41, and it was $4.365 on October 5.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). One search summary put the August monthly average at $4.19, which doesn't fit with these weekly figures, so that number is unverified.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, up from 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3% after 0.2% in July. The gasoline index rose 3.9% in August, more than a third of the monthly all-items increase. Annual inflation stayed at 3.4%, the same as July.

The headline 12-month change BLS reports is calculated from not seasonally adjusted index levels and rounded to one decimal. So the September 12-month figure depends on the unadjusted August-to-September change, not the seasonally adjusted monthly figure.

Georgia is 2-14 in games played in Tuscaloosa. Its last win there was 26-23 in overtime on Sept 22, 2007, which SI/Hot Augusta also report. Alabama won the last two Tuscaloosa meetings: 41-24 in 2020 and 41-34 in 2024.

In the 38-14 win over Vanderbilt, Georgia QB Gunner Stockton went 25 of 32 for a season-high 295 yards and 3 TDs. Georgia ran for 176 yards on 34 carries and held Vanderbilt to 293 total yards, 61 of them in the second half. Vanderbilt was playing its backup QB.
Gunner Stockton, a fifth-year player, has started all five Georgia games. Wikipedia reports no significant Georgia injuries through Week 5.

Before the Mississippi State game, Kalen DeBoer said right tackle Jayvin James was questionable with a lower-extremity injury from the South Carolina game. He also said William Sanders had an upper-body injury and was expected to play. Linebackers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu were out, with Umeozulu out longer. Reports describe Alabama's offensive line as banged up. No status update for Georgia week was found.
President Trump announced he will attend the game in Tuscaloosa. It is the third straight year the two teams meet in the regular season.

Seasonally adjusted month-over-month core CPI in 2026: Feb +0.2%, Mar +0.2%, Apr +0.4%, May +0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul +0.2%, Aug +0.3%. August came in one-tenth above most estimates.

The month leaving the 12-month window is September 2025. In that month the core index rose 0.2% seasonally adjusted and 3.0% over 12 months. The 12-month change for September 2026 will roughly hold at the August level if the September 2026 core monthly gain is close to September 2025's gain, and move up or down if it is larger or smaller.
Shelter, the largest core component, rose 0.3% in August 2026 after two straight monthly gains of 0.1%. It was up 3.0% year over year.

market.question: Will average **gas prices** be above $4.00? (Above 4.00)
market.rules: If average regular gas prices for the United States are strictly greater than $4.00 on Nov 3, 2026 according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.fact: AAA's national average for regular gas was $4.3653 on Oct 5, 2026. It was $4.3697 the day before, $4.4768 a week earlier, $4.1459 a month earlier and $3.1339 a year earlier. The average sits about 11.5 cents above the $4.25 threshold.

On Oct 1 the national average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents from $4.48 a week earlier. WTI settled at $90.42, EIA gasoline demand fell to 8.68 million barrels a day, and U.S. crude stocks rose 0.9 million barrels to 427.3 million.

September 2026 averaged $4.33 a gallon, a record for the month and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023. AAA said prices were the highest they had ever been for this time of year.
Gasoline futures fell 1.8% to $3.25 a gallon on Oct 5, 2026. Crude oil fell 0.53% to $90.62 a barrel, which is down 2.59% over the past month but 46.9% higher than a year ago.

Crude oil fell to about $90 a barrel on Oct 5 as signs of more global supply outweighed Middle East risks. The previous Friday, G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves.

Georgia has a 30-day suspension of its 33.3-cent gas tax that runs through Oct 29, and its prices are down 34–38 cents. Ohio announced a 90-day suspension on Sept 30 that runs to the end of the year, and its prices are down 39–43 cents.

Indiana suspended its state gas tax and has the nation's lowest prices at $3.74. Kentucky and Illinois cut or paused tax increases, and California and Michigan allowed early use of winter-blend gasoline. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan called the decline 'not exactly the most organic' because refineries behind the Strait of Hormuz still cannot fully move their products.
Georgia's gas tax holiday is due to end Oct 29, five days before the Nov 3 resolution date, unless it is extended again. Ohio's suspension runs past Nov 3.

Crude moving through Hormuz reached a 7-day average of 13.5 million barrels a day, back to the prewar level and up from about 6–8 million in mid-September. Refined product shipments were only 677,000 barrels a day, against 3.6 million before the war.

Foreign Policy reported that oil is flowing out of the Strait of Hormuz again, but refinery damage and disrupted shipping are expected to keep gasoline and diesel prices high. Tanker freight rates have risen about twentyfold since the war began.

GasBuddy's pre-war seasonal pattern for 2026 had prices falling through the fall to a yearly low in December. This reflects the usual autumn decline after the switch to winter-blend gasoline, which typically happens in mid-September.
AAA updates its national average for regular gasoline daily, quoted to four decimal places. The question resolves Yes only if the Nov 3, 2026 figure is strictly greater than $4.25.

An endorsement requires a clear, affirmative statement of support for the nominee's election. Positive comments without explicit support, policy endorsements without nominee endorsement, or conditional endorsements do not qualify. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. Sarcastic statements or those immediately clarified as jokes do not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: Right after the March 2026 Texas primary, Sanders said he would campaign for Talarico in Texas 'if asked.' When Talarico approached Senate Democrats for support before the primary, Sanders said it was 'too early' to say whether he would endorse him.

The Tribune's preview of the convention says Sanders was headlining to build excitement for Talarico and the down-ballot ticket. It contains no endorsement statement or direct quote from Sanders about Talarico, and Gov. Abbott used Sanders' appearance to attack Democrats as too far left.

Sanders' 2026 Senate endorsements include Graham Platner (Maine), Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan) and Peggy Flanagan (Minnesota). He also endorsed Florida nominee Angie Nixon on 2026-08-20, two days after she won her primary. Talarico won the Texas nomination in March and had not been endorsed as of the latest reports.
VTDigger reports that Sanders' 2026 endorsement criteria favor progressive candidates who run strong grassroots campaigns and want to challenge the establishment status quo.

In a September interview with TIME, Talarico rejected the socialist label and gave his own definition of capitalism. Republicans have attacked him for backing a 'Democrat Socialist agenda.' The article does not mention Sanders in connection with Talarico.

In mid-September, Sen. Ted Cruz warned that Talarico would model himself after Bernie Sanders and be 'the most woke left-wing senator the country has ever seen.' Republicans are using Sanders as a line of attack against Talarico. The date is approximate.
Talarico and Republican nominee Ken Paxton launched dueling ads in early October in what the Post calls a heated general-election race.
The general election between Talarico and Paxton is on 2026-11-03, the day the question closes, which leaves about four weeks for an endorsement. No scheduled joint Sanders–Talarico event was found.

('uninspiring' direction) and DawsOn. None were outright negative.

World of Reel's first reaction called the film a timely indictment of Facebook but asked 'where's the cinema?', faulting the filmmaking more than the script.

The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

market.question: Will there be more than 30 transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026? (Above 30)
market.rules:
If the number of transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz as reported by the IMF PortWatch is above 30 from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The total is calculated by summing daily counts from Sep 28, 2026 to Oct 4, 2026. The market will resolve no earlier than Tuesday at 9 AM following the end of the period, once complete data is available.

recent_facts.fact: As of 2026-10-05, the IMF PortWatch 7-day average for the Strait of Hormuz was about 3 commercial ships per day. That is roughly 21 transits a week, against a pre-crisis norm of about 85 a day. The latest daily figure shown is 1 transit on 2026-09-27.
The Oct 4 brief says IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, the most recent published day, against a baseline of 85 a day. It gives no PortWatch daily counts for Sep 28–Oct 4 yet.

IMF PortWatch publishes weekly, usually on Tuesday, with about a two-day lag. Its counts come from AIS signals, so ships that go dark or are jammed are missed and its counts run lower than other trackers.

Straits.live reported 8 vessels transited on October 1, against a baseline of about 88 a day, and said 4 of the 8 had AIS transponders switched off. This is not a PortWatch figure, and PortWatch, which relies on AIS, would likely miss the dark ships.

A tracker summary cites PortWatch-based AIS-visible traffic averaging 6.1 ships a day over a recent week (day 219 of the crisis), or 43 crossings: 16 tankers, 27 cargo ships and no LNG/LPG carriers. The exact week covered is unclear.
PortWatch recorded a single transit on 2026-09-20. Reuters commodity-vessel counts, which use a different method, were 7 on Sep 22 and 10 on Sep 23, with a 10-day moving average of about 17.

recent_facts.source: Search summary (likely Lloyd's List transit monitor, not PortWatch)
recent_facts.fact: A non-PortWatch tracker reported 114 transits for Sep 21–27 and 137 for Sep 14–20, which counts much higher than PortWatch's roughly 3 a day. I couldn't confirm which provider produced this figure, so treat it as unverified.
Iranian media (Fars) claimed the IRGC targeted seven tankers in the strait over five days. As of Oct 4, 247 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Hormuz area.

At least six vessels were struck in the strait in the week before Oct 4, including a Kuwait-flagged tanker on Oct 1. Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd have suspended transits, and six P&I clubs have withdrawn cover.
Iran said in October that the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until its demands are met.
On Sep 23, CENTCOM said 115 commercial vessels had been redirected under the US blockade, which resumed on July 14. US–Iran talks on a phased arrangement had not settled the two sides' differences.
PortWatch daily data for Sep 28–Oct 4 should appear in the weekly update, usually on Tuesday (Oct 6). The question closes 2026-10-06 13:00 UTC.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: The FOMC unanimously raised rates by 25 bp to 3.75–4.00% on September 16, 2026, its first hike since 2023. Three members had favored a hike at the July meeting. The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%.

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams said in separate speeches that the Fed has time to assess the economy before considering another rate increase. These remarks were reported as reducing investor expectations of an October hike.
A Bloomberg report published October 2 had the headline 'Fed may skip October but pull U.S. rate hike trigger in December'.

In late September, before the weak jobs data: Williams (Sept 24) called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'. Paulson (Sept 24) said further hikes may be needed. Hammack (Sept 25) warned an 'inflationary mindset could start to set in'. Governor Cook (Sept 28) said the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'.

Warsh described the September move as having 'removed a dose of accommodation'. He has avoided signaling where rates go next. Higher energy prices tied to the Iran war were cited as one reason for the hike.
September 2026 CPI is due October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the FOMC meeting. September PCE is due later in October.

facts_dropped.fact: The Fed's official rate-change table shows the target range moved from 3.50–3.75% (set December 11, 2025) to 3.75–4.00% effective September 17, 2026. That is a 25 bp increase and the only change so far in 2026. The current upper bound is 4.00%.

facts_dropped.fact: The September jobs report showed payrolls up only 29,000, against forecasts of 80,000–100,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% and wage growth slowed.

facts_dropped.fact: August PCE prices rose 0.3% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year. Core PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y, below the 3.3% forecast.

market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: Channel 13 poll, fielded Sept 30 (n=1,103, MoE 2.5%): Netanyahu bloc 54 seats (Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 8, UTJ 8, Shas 7, Religious Zionism 7). Opposition Jewish bloc 52 (Yashar 21, Together 11, Democrats 11, Yisrael Beiteinu 9). Arab parties 14. Neither bloc reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority.
Maariv poll: Netanyahu bloc 51 seats, opposition 53, Likud 19, Otzma Yehudit 9. The Netanyahu bloc gained 2 seats from Maariv's previous poll and neither camp reaches 61.

Late-September polls disagree on Netanyahu's bloc total. Channel 14: 63 (Likud 32). i24NEWS: 60 (Likud 27). Zman Yisrael: 53. Channel 13: 51. N12: 50. Maariv: 49. Yashar is at 22-23 in most of them. The Reservists party is placed in different blocs by different pollsters, which moves bloc totals by several seats.

The election is set for October 27, 2026, after the Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026 at the end of its full term. The threshold is 3.25% and 61 of 120 seats are needed for a majority. Netanyahu is the incumbent PM and Likud's candidate, with New Hope merged into Likud.

The question resolves only on a PM formally sworn in after the 2026 election; a caretaker PM does not count. If Netanyahu stays on as caretaker during coalition talks, that is not a swearing-in. If nobody is sworn in by Dec 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The question closes Oct 28, 2026, one day after the vote.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: after the Nov 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu's government was sworn in on Dec 29, 2022, about 58 days later. Israeli government formation usually takes weeks to months, so no swearing-in would be expected by the Oct 28 close.

UNVERIFIED, recalled from memory: of the 6 Knesset elections from 2015 to 2022, the PM sworn in directly after the vote was Netanyahu after 2015, 2020 and 2022, and Bennett after 2021. The April 2019 and Sept 2019 elections produced no government and led to repeat elections.

On Sept 23 the Central Elections Committee disqualified Ra'am and the Joint List. The Supreme Court overturned that on Oct 2, and on Oct 4 it rejected further disqualification appeals. Petitions against Otzma Yehudit were rejected on Sept 24.

Bennett said he is willing to give up the premiership in a post-Netanyahu government. The opposition Jewish parties (Yashar, Together, Democrats, Yisrael Beiteinu) have said they won't form a coalition that includes Arab parties. Lieberman has not endorsed any PM candidate.
Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg ordered Netanyahu to remove campaign videos that made unauthorized use of the IDF and public resources.

Netanyahu is under pressure over a Wall Street Journal report that Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel warned him by phone days before the Oct 7, 2023 attack. On Oct 3, Eisenkot connected Netanyahu's rejection of a state inquiry to a flydubai near-disaster.

Election day is Oct 27, 2026. After that the President consults with parties and assigns a candidate to form a government, and the new government must win a Knesset vote and be sworn in. Under the question's rules, this has to happen by Dec 31, 2027.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 3, 2026, the US naval blockade of Iran was still in force, and Trump was sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Diplomacy was reported as deadlocked.

Preliminary tanker-tracking estimates showed Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first such month since the war began in February.

Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal, under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade, removed oil sanctions and reinstated a regional ceasefire. Trump said Iran had 'overplayed their hand' but said he expected talks to resume that week.

On October 4, Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran was still reviewing a US counterproposal, sent through intermediaries. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said it was 'in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues.' FM Araghchi said there is 'no military solution.'

The two sides disagree on what comes first. Iran insists the Hormuz and US blockade issues be settled first, while Washington insists on nuclear concessions. Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive the talks.

Trump said he was 'open to a deal, but not to the one the Iranians offered.' He reportedly told officials he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. The US also launched an expanded sanctions regime, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' in August 2026.

An IRGC advisor claimed that no US naval vessels are now in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman, and that US warships have pulled back 1,000 km. This is an Iranian claim; no official US announcement about the blockade accompanied it.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June MOU, including ending the naval blockade. Araghchi said the strait could reopen within seven days if those conditions are met.

Precedent: the first blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026 (about 66 days). On June 14 Trump said he had 'authorized lifting the US naval blockade' once an accord was reached. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18. That is one prior instance, so this is an unverified base rate.
The second blockade phase began July 14–15, 2026, after Trump's July 13 announcement, and was about 83 days old as of October 5. More than 100 vessels had been redirected by September 12.

No signed agreement or scheduled formal US-Iran negotiating session was reported before October 31. The next known date is the US midterm election on November 3, after which Trump reportedly expects renewed bombing.

Only an official, unambiguous US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts. Iranian claims, leaks, partial exemptions for specific vessels, and naval repositioning without an announcement do not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 3, 2026, the US naval blockade of Iran was still in force, and Trump was sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Diplomacy was reported as deadlocked.

Preliminary tanker-tracking estimates showed Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first such month since the war began in February.

Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal, under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade, removed oil sanctions and reinstated a regional ceasefire. Trump said Iran had 'overplayed their hand' but said he expected talks to resume that week.

On October 4, Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran was still reviewing a US counterproposal, sent through intermediaries. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said it was 'in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues.' FM Araghchi said there is 'no military solution.'

The two sides disagree on what comes first. Iran insists the Hormuz and US blockade issues be settled first, while Washington insists on nuclear concessions. Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive the talks.

Trump said he was 'open to a deal, but not to the one the Iranians offered.' He reportedly told officials he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. The US also launched an expanded sanctions regime, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' in August 2026.

An IRGC advisor claimed that no US naval vessels are now in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman, and that US warships have pulled back 1,000 km. This is an Iranian claim; no official US announcement about the blockade accompanied it.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June MOU, including ending the naval blockade. Araghchi said the strait could reopen within seven days if those conditions are met.

Precedent: the first blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026 (about 66 days). On June 14 Trump said he had 'authorized lifting the US naval blockade' once an accord was reached. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18. That is one prior instance, so this is an unverified base rate.
The second blockade phase began July 14–15, 2026, after Trump's July 13 announcement, and was about 83 days old as of October 5. More than 100 vessels had been redirected by September 12.

No signed agreement or scheduled formal US-Iran negotiating session was reported before October 31. The next known date is the US midterm election on November 3, after which Trump reportedly expects renewed bombing.

Only an official, unambiguous US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts. Iranian claims, leaks, partial exemptions for specific vessels, and naval repositioning without an announcement do not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: Tampa Bay beat the Yankees 1-0 in ALDS Game 1 on Oct 3, 2026 (attendance 40,542, game time 2:30). The Rays lead the best-of-five series 1-0, so they need two more wins and the Yankees need three.

In Game 1, Drew Rasmussen struck out 10 over eight innings and took a no-hitter into the eighth. Jonathan Aranda's third-inning solo homer off Gerrit Cole was the only run, and Bryan Baker pitched a 1-2-3 ninth.
CBS Sports' Game 1 recap headline says a baserunning decision by Yankees catcher Austin Wells doomed New York in the 1-0 loss.

Remaining schedule: Game 2 Mon Oct 5 at Tampa Bay, 8 PM ET; Game 3 Wed Oct 7 at Yankee Stadium; Game 4 (if needed) Thu Oct 8 at Yankee Stadium; Game 5 (if needed) Sat Oct 10 at Tampa Bay. Tampa Bay's home games are at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg.
Game 2 starters: Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA, 0.92 WHIP, 239 K) against Rays RHP Freddy Peralta (10-11, 4.42 ERA, 1.32 WHIP, 156 K). As of research time, Game 2 had not been played.

MLB.com calls Schlittler the likely AL Cy Young winner and says he had a 1.16 road ERA. Peralta went 5-0 with a 0.79 ERA over his final six starts. Rasmussen went 16-5 with the AL's best WHIP (0.91) and has a career 5-2 record and 1.81 ERA in 11 appearances against New York.

Game 3 starters were not confirmed. Carlos Rodón is possible for New York, and Peralta or Nick Martinez for Tampa Bay; Martinez has a 2.38 road ERA versus 3.90 at home. Griffin Jax (no runs allowed... one run in his last 18 innings over four outings) was also a starting option for the Rays.

Regular season: Tampa Bay went 98-64 and won the AL East, earning a first-round bye. New York went 93-68 and finished 2nd in the AL East. The source says the teams played 15 times with Tampa Bay leading 8-6, which doesn't add up, so the exact head-to-head is unconfirmed.
Aaron Judge is not on the Yankees' ALDS roster. He has a moderate right-calf (soleus) strain from Sept 16 and also missed the Wild Card Series. He could be added for a potential ALCS.

Other injuries. Rays: Gavin Lux (60-day IL, shoulder), Shane McClanahan (15-day IL, forearm), Griffin Jax (day-to-day, back). Yankees: Clarke Schmidt (15-day IL, biceps), Fernando Cruz (60-day IL, elbow).
The Yankees reached the ALDS by sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card Series, winning Game 2 by 9-2.

England beat Czech Republic 2–0 away in Prague on 29 September 2026 in Nations League Matchday 2, with goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane. This was the reverse fixture of Tuesday's game.

England lost 3–2 to Spain at Wembley on 26 September 2026 in Matchday 1, with Gordon and Kane scoring. After 3 games England have 6 points (W2 L1) in Nations League Group A3, and Spain have 9.

Czechia have lost all 3 of their Nations League group games: 1–2 to Croatia, 0–2 to England and 1–3 to Spain. Goal also lists earlier results of a 1–1 draw with South Africa and a 0–3 defeat to Mexico.
Goal reports Ladislav Krejčí is suspended for Czechia after his red card against Spain, and that no other Czech injuries or suspensions are listed.

England left-back Nico O'Reilly, Tuchel's first choice, was ruled out of the Czechia game injured. Reports name Rio Ngumoha and/or Rico Lewis as his replacement; sources differ. Ezri Konsa was a minor fitness doubt, and reports conflict on whether he is fit.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 31?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Unnamed people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the East-West pipeline is still running normally after reports of a new weekend strike on a pumping station near Khurais. Saudi Aramco and the Energy Ministry did not immediately answer Bloomberg's requests for comment. The 'operating normally' claim comes from those sources, not from the government.

Reports say that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Aramco has said anything publicly about the pipeline since it was attacked in September. Every report of a restart or higher flows so far comes from anonymous sources or market-intelligence firms.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia raised flows on the 7 million b/d East-West pipeline to more than 80% of capacity, close to 6 million b/d, with about 4.5 million b/d available for export. These figures came from tanker-tracking and market data such as Kepler, not from a government statement.

Anonymous Reuters sources said the pipeline restarted on September 22 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million b/d. The article cites no statement from the government or the Ministry of Energy.

The Ministry of Energy said in an official SPA statement that the East-West pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after several drone attacks on September 10 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The ministry said teams were taking steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.
The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, carried out by several drones from Iraq, saying it caused injuries and 'some damage that is currently being addressed.'

Precedent from earlier in 2026: after attacks in April cut flows on the East-West pipeline, the Ministry of Energy announced through SPA on April 12 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has publicly confirmed restorations before. This is a single case.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the closure would be a short interruption lasting days. He is a US official, not part of the Saudi government, so his statement does not count toward resolution.

Sources gave different repair estimates: one said five to six weeks, another said sooner. After the September 22 restart, Reuters sources said getting back to full capacity would likely take at least six to eight weeks.

The question resolves Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is currently operating, at any capacity, by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Anonymous-source reports like the Reuters and Bloomberg pieces do not count, and neither do statements about future or planned resumption. Based on what was found, no qualifying government statement has been reported as of October 5.

About 26 days remain before the deadline (October 31, 11:59 PM ET; the question closes November 1, 03:59 UTC). No scheduled ministry briefing on the pipeline was found. Attacks are continuing, including the reported strike near Khurais on the weekend of October 3–4.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $80 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić be the next Prime Minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: An early parliamentary election for all 250 National Assembly seats is set for 25 October 2026, after Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 September. Seats are allocated by closed-list PR with d'Hondt and a 3% threshold, which is waived for minority parties. A majority is 126 seats.

Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist and medical professor born in 1970, heads the ballot for the 'Student List – Students Are Winning' in the 2026 election. Reporting describes him as the Student List's lead candidate for prime minister.
Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister. He heads SNS's 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list.

Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister on 3 October at Belgrade Arena and promised a 'comprehensive' victory. Al Jazeera reports that if SNS wins a majority, parliament would elect Vučić as PM. It describes the Student List as the main challenger.
A Faktor Plus poll had Vučić's United Serbia at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%. That was a 5.6-point gain for the Student List.
An NSPM poll presented by Vukadinović had the Student List at 44.4% and United Serbia at 41.7%. The exact publication date is approximate: late September or early October 2026.
A CRTA survey found 44% of respondents backing the Student List and 32% backing Vučić's bloc. The publication date is approximate: September 2026.
Speaking from New York, Vučić was reported as saying the Student List leads and is 'hard to catch'.
Another poll had the Student List at 39.6% and SNS at 37.5%. Wikipedia sums up recent polling as a tightened race in which results vary by pollster.

Other lists include European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš), Authentic Right (Miloš Jovanović) and the SPS-led Factor of Stability (Ivica Dačić). SSP said it would cooperate with the Student List. PSG dropped out of the race to back the Student List.
Election day is 25 October 2026, the same day this question closes. A PM can only be elected later, after the new Assembly holds its constitutive session.

After the 17 December 2023 election, the new Assembly first met on 6 February 2024 and the President named Vučević PM-designate on 30 March. The government was elected on 2 May 2024, about 4.5 months after the vote, with 152 votes in favour.

Under Serbian procedure, the President gives the mandate to a PM-designate, and the Assembly then elects the PM and cabinet by a majority of all 250 MPs, meaning 126 votes. Vučić has resigned, so who will give the mandate after the vote is not confirmed in these sources (unverified).

If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.
