market.question: Will CPI rise more than 0.5% in September 2026? (Above 0.5%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% (single-decimal) in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will always close at 8:25 AM ET on the scheduled day of the data release (October 14, 2026). Please note: the Expiration Value is the single-decimal value published at the Source Agency. In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August 2026, after 0.1% in July. Over 12 months, all items rose 3.4% before seasonal adjustment.

In August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the all-items increase. Energy rose 2.1%, food 0.1%, shelter 0.3% and core (less food and energy) 0.3%, up from 0.2% in July.

Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items CPI changes in 2026: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. That is 2 of 7 months above 0.5%, 3 of 7 above 0.4%, and 1 of 7 above 0.6%.

AAA's September 2026 average for regular gasoline was $4.33 a gallon, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). On Oct 1 the national average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents on the week, with crude back in the $90 per barrel range.

The August 2026 national average gas price was $4.19 a gallon, using EIA data. This is a different provider from AAA, so comparing it with AAA's $4.33 September average (roughly +3%) is only approximate.

AAA's weekly national averages in September 2026: $4.14 (Sep 3), $4.27 (Sep 10), $4.43 (Sep 17), $4.48 (Sep 24). AAA said $4.48 was the highest ever for that time of year, driven by volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude prices.
August 2026 was the most expensive August ever at the pump, with the national average above $4 every day of the month. The previous August record average was $3.97 (2022).

Gasoline CPI was up 27.4% year over year in August 2026, and core CPI was up 2.4% year over year. Gas prices had been $2.98 a gallon on Feb 28, 2026, before U.S. military operations against Iran began.
BLS is scheduled to publish the September 2026 CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

The headline figure is the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change in CPI-U, rounded to one decimal. For the seasonal factors introduced in January 2026, BLS used intervention-analysis seasonal adjustment on 57 series, including motor fuels.

Precedent: in the Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2025 shutdown (43 days), BLS pushed the September 2025 CPI back from Oct 15 to Oct 24 so Social Security could meet its COLA deadlines, and it cancelled the October 2025 CPI. My searches found no reporting of a 2026 shutdown affecting BLS (unverified).

market.rules:

The market will close at 8:29 AM on the day of the expected release of the data. The market will expire at the first 10:00 AM following the release of the data for Q3 2026, or 3 months following that expected date of data release. Please note the Expiration Value is the one-decimal value published by the BEA.

recent_facts.fact: Over the quarter the GDPNow Q3 2026 nowcast started at 5.0% in late July, was 4.4% on September 10, rose to 5.1% on September 16–17, and was 5.0% on September 25.

recent_facts.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Nowcast (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: In early October 2026 the New York Fed Staff Nowcast for 2026:Q3 GDP growth was 2.2%, down 0.3 percentage point after new data releases. It had been 2.3% in late September. The exact date was not confirmed because the page did not render.
For Q2 2026, GDPNow's final nowcast was 1.5% and the BEA advance estimate was also 1.5%, matching after rounding. This is a single quarter, so it is unverified as a general accuracy rate.
Real PCE rose 0.6% (month over month) in August 2026, and nominal PCE rose 0.9%, the most since March. July's nominal PCE gain was revised down to 0.1%.

The July 2026 goods and services trade deficit was $88.6 billion, up $17.4 billion from $71.2 billion in June. Exports fell $6.6 billion to $310.7 billion and imports rose $10.8 billion to $399.3 billion.

In the third estimate, Q2 2026 real GDP grew at a 2.2% annual rate, revised up 0.7 point from 1.5%. Q1 2026 growth was 2.5%. The release included the 2026 annual update, which revised data from Q1 2021 through Q1 2026.

The BEA will release the Q3 2026 GDP Advance Estimate on October 29, 2026 at 8:30 AM, along with September Personal Income and Outlays. The August trade report comes out October 6, and the Q3 second estimate is due November 25.
A continuing resolution signed September 2, 2026 funds the federal government through December 11, 2026, so no shutdown should interrupt BEA's October 29 release.
The question resolves on the one-decimal, seasonally adjusted annualized real GDP growth rate in BEA's Advance Estimate. It needs a value above 2.0, so a reading of exactly 2.0 resolves No.

recent_facts.fact: The August 2026 CPI-U (all items, not seasonally adjusted) index was 334.980, up 3.4% over 12 months. The seasonally adjusted monthly rise was 0.4%. Over 12 months, energy was up 16.3%, gasoline up 27.4%, food up 2.7%, and core up 2.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U index was 324.800, up 3.0% over 12 months and up 0.3% for the month before seasonal adjustment. This is the year-ago base. Derived from the BLS levels: September 2026 needs an index of at least about 336.33 (up about 0.40% unadjusted from August) to round to 3.6%, and at least about 336.66 (up about 0.50%) to round to 3.7%.
BLS plans to release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA's weekly national average gasoline price rose through September 2026: $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and $4.48 on Sept 24. AAA called Sept 24 the highest ever for that time of year. On Sept 17 it was more than $1 above a year earlier.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). One search summary put the August monthly average at $4.19, which doesn't fit with these weekly figures, so that number is unverified.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, up from 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3% after 0.2% in July. The gasoline index rose 3.9% in August, more than a third of the monthly all-items increase. Annual inflation stayed at 3.4%, the same as July.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In 270toWin's average of the 5 most recent general-election polls, Democrat James Talarico has 49.6% and Republican Ken Paxton has 45.6%. Talarico leads in all 10 polls the site lists from Sept. 10 to Oct. 3, 2026, by between 1 and 6 points.

A Siena College poll released Oct. 3, 2026 (615 likely voters, ±4.5%) has Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 45%. Siena's earlier poll, released Sept. 17 (614 likely voters), had Talarico 49% to Paxton 43%.
A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters (±3%) has Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, inside the margin of error. Talarico's favorability is 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable. Paxton's is 40% to 58%.

Pulse Decision Science, a conservative polling firm, surveyed 800 likely voters Sept. 24–27 and found Paxton at 48% and Talarico at 45%. It was the first poll in weeks to show Paxton ahead. Undecided voters fell from 11% in May to 4%.
A Marist poll of 1,139 Texas registered voters (Sept. 17–20, ±4.4%) has Talarico at 50% and Paxton at 44%. Talarico gets 55% among independents.

Other recent polls: Texas Public Opinion Research, Talarico 49% to Paxton 44%; Texas Southern University, 47% to 46%; Trafalgar, 46% to 45%; Emerson, 47% to 46%; Mason-Dixon, 46% to 43%; InsiderAdvantage, 47% to 46%.

Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026. The questions close Nov. 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC, which is election night.

The last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988, so Republicans have won every Texas Senate election since. Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office since 1994.

Texas polls understated the Democrat in 2018, were close in 2022, and understated the Republican Senate margin in 2020 and 2024. In 2024, final averages had Cruz ahead by about 4 points and Emerson's final poll had him up 48–47, but he won by 8.5.

market.question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: According to IMF PortWatch, Bab el-Mandeb traffic averaged 28 vessels/day in August 2026, the lowest monthly level in the recent series. A 3-day sample to about 11 September averaged about 26/day (79 vessels), and the 7-day moving average was 24/day on 29 July.

A late-September update said IMF PortWatch recorded a single transit for 20 September, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85/day. It did not say whether this was a preliminary or lagged figure, and it gave no 7-day average. Neither the figure nor which strait it refers to has been checked against PortWatch.

recent_facts.source: Search summary of late-September shipping reports (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Reports summarized in search results said IMF PortWatch AIS data for Bab el-Mandeb in mid-to-late September 2026 showed daily volumes in the low-to-mid 20s, with about 22 vessels on recent days. This has not been checked against the PortWatch page itself.

Lloyd's List Intelligence's own Red Sea Transit Monitor counted 290 preliminary Bab el-Mandeb transits for 21–27 September 2026 (264 the week before), a 4-week weekly average of 280, against 316 in June and 257 in January. This counting method differs from PortWatch's and gives higher numbers.
In early to mid September 2026, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast down to the Bab el-Mandeb, including the port of Mocha. Other reports say they also took Perim Island and the Hanish Islands.
Windward reported that Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from 35 daily transits before the Houthi advance to 25 after. Traffic then recovered, reaching 45 transits on one Sunday in mid-September.

The Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline in September 2026 and said Saudi shipping using the strait would be targeted. There have been 12 Houthi attacks or attempted attacks on commercial vessels in the southern Red Sea since July 2026.
The Houthis told the EU in a letter that they would not target European ships in the Red Sea and that their activity would not affect navigation through Bab el-Mandeb.

On 4 October 2026, the Saudi-led coalition pledged support for a Yemeni government offensive against the Houthis. ABC News reported the same day that the Houthis targeted a Saudi oil facility as hostilities escalated.

The Houthi blockade on Saudi Arabia, imposed on 20 July 2026, reduced crude exports through the Yanbu terminals. The Saudi pipeline has resumed at reduced rates, and some operators are increasingly sending ships back through the Red Sea.
A Houthi missile attack on the Egyptian cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab el-Mandeb on 11 August 2026 killed four to six crew. The PortWatch monthly average stayed at 28/day for August.

recent_facts.source: Anadolu Agency (citing IMF PortWatch / World Bank)
recent_facts.fact: PortWatch daily averages: about 71/day from January 2022 to October 2023; 43/day from 17 November 2023 to 19 February 2024; about 33.5/day in 2025; 34–37/day in January–July 2026; 28/day in August 2026. None of the figures found here comes close to a 7-day average of 10 or below, including through the 2024–2025 Houthi campaign. This is not a full check of PortWatch's daily series.

The question resolves Yes if PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of Bab el-Mandeb transit calls of 10 or below for any date through 31 October 2026. PortWatch counts AIS-visible transits, so ships with AIS off are not counted. Revisions are considered only until the 31 October data is published.
PortWatch daily data is published with a lag. Data for dates up to 31 October must appear within 14 days after that date, and the question closes on 1 November 2026 (03:59 UTC).

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: To win a Senate majority, Democrats need to pick up four Republican-held seats while holding the three seats of their own that are seriously contested, including Michigan. Republicans currently control the chamber. Vice President Vance is a Republican, so a 50-50 split resolves to Republican control under the rules.

CNN's October ranking puts North Carolina (open seat, Tillis retiring) as the seat most likely to flip, with Democrat Roy Cooper up 11 points over Republican Michael Whatley among likely voters in an Elon University/YouGov poll released in September. Ohio is No. 2 and Maine No. 3. Kansas joins the list for the first time, making it 10 seats.

In Texas, a New York Times/Siena poll has Democrat James Talarico leading Republican Ken Paxton 51% to 45%. In the Ohio special election, a NYT/Siena poll has Democrat Sherrod Brown leading Republican Sen. Jon Husted 49% to 46%.

RealClearPolitics polling averages show Democratic Senate candidates ahead by about 8 points in North Carolina, 3 in Texas and 3 in Ohio. Forbes reports Democrats lead the polls in NC, TX, MI, ME and AK.

In Maine, Republican Sen. Susan Collins is tied 50%-50% with Democrat Troy Jackson in a CBS News/YouGov poll. A University of New Hampshire poll from the previous month had Jackson ahead 51% to 47% among likely voters. Collins is the only GOP senator running in a state Harris won in 2024.

Alaska polls are mixed. A Quantus Insights poll has Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan ahead of Democrat Mary Peltola 48-47. Newsweek reports a poll giving Peltola a 7-point lead, and some polls show her ahead after ranked-choice reallocation.
In Iowa's open seat, Democrat Turek averages 48.0% to Republican Ashley Hinson's 46.4%. Fox News has Turek ahead 49-47 and Rasmussen Reports has him ahead 47-43.

In Nebraska, independent Dan Osborn and Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts are tied 47%-47% among likely voters. Six major public surveys show the race either statistically tied or with Osborn narrowly ahead. Exact poll dates were not confirmed.

recent_facts.source: Resolution rules (market text); Osborn caucus stance recalled from memory, UNVERIFIED
recent_facts.fact: Independents count toward a party only if they formally caucus with it or announce an intent to. If caucus decisions are unclear on election day, the market can stay open until January 4. Osborn has said he would not caucus with either party (recalled from memory, unverified), so a seat he wins might not count for Democrats.
In Michigan's open Democratic-held seat, a Fox News poll has Democrat Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Republican Mike Rogers 50-49, and a Marist poll has El-Sayed ahead 51-44.

In Georgia, Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff leads Republican Rep. Mike Collins 51.6% to 41.8% in the Pollsmax average. Fox News had Ossoff ahead 56-43 among registered voters, and YouGov had him ahead 51-41.
In New Hampshire's open Democratic-held seat, Democrat Chris Pappas leads Republican John E. Sununu 47.7% to 41.3% in the RCP average. One recent poll had Pappas ahead 50-42.

As of October 2026, US Polling Data's generic congressional ballot tracker shows Democrats at 49.3% and Republicans at 41.9% (D+7.4). Trump's approval is 37.3% approve and 60.3% disapprove, and Quartz reports his approval at a record low.

Election day is November 3, 2026, and the questions close November 4 at 04:59 UTC. Seats up include the regular class plus special elections in Ohio and Florida. Runoffs, such as a possible Georgia runoff if no one passes 50%, decide their seats even if held after November.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: Front-month WTI crude was at $89.08/bbl on October 5, 2026, down $2.03 (-2.23%) on the day, with an intraday low of $88.93. It was down 4.25% over the month and up 44.4% year on year.

On October 5 (13:10 quote), NYMEX WTI futures traded at $88.90 for Nov 2026 (CLX26), $87.73 for Dec 2026 (CLZ26) and $86.72 for Jan 2027. The curve is in backwardation, with December about $1.17 below November.

NYMEX Nov'26 WTI expires October 20, 2026. Under the ICE rule (5 US business days before the 25th, because Oct 25 is a Sunday), ICE Nov WTI's last trade would be about Oct 19. That would make December the Pyth 'Active Month' from about the Oct 15 session (opening 8 PM ET Oct 14). These dates are derived, not confirmed on the ICE expiry page.

WTI settled at $91.11 on Friday, October 2, down $1.76 from Thursday's $92.87 settlement. The drop followed a European agreement to release emergency diesel stocks under a G7/IEA plan of about 100 million barrels.
On October 1, WTI jumped nearly 3% to $92.87 after a U.S. aircraft carrier deployment. EnergyNow also cited China's suspension of fuel exports and renewed U.S.-Iran military concerns that day.

Oil fell on October 5 as Middle East crude exports rose and the G7 released about 100 million barrels of reserves. Higher loadings through the Strait of Hormuz and continued operation of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline eased supply concerns. Brent was about $102.40 and WTI about $90.65.

Saudi Aramco cut its November Arab Light price to Asia to $5 below the regional benchmark as Middle Eastern flows normalize. Saudi-backed forces in Yemen launched operations against Houthi areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and OPEC+ kept quotas unchanged.
WTI closed at $96.05 on September 9, 2026, its highest close since May 22. Oil rose more than 8% in September as the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes.

Recent swings were large. WTI closed at $82.49 on Jul 17 and $92.19 on Jul 23 (+6% that day on Red Sea tanker attacks), then $82.61 on Jul 27 (-7.5%). It fell from $96.02 on Jun 3 to $69.63 on Jun 24.

On September 8, oil rose to $99 (headline figure, likely Brent) on a report that Iran launched a second undisclosed attack on U.S. Navy ships. WTI's highest close since late May was $96.05, so WTI has not been confirmed above $100 since May.
WTI closed at $96.02 on June 3 after Netanyahu said the U.S. and Israel might strike Iran again. No WTI close at or above $105 appears in the June–October 2026 chronology.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. recent_facts.fact: A CBS News poll of 1,144 Maine registered voters, fielded Sept 23–Oct 1, 2026 (MOE ±4.7), shows Republican Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson tied. 10% of voters are undecided, and 10% say they could still change their minds.
A NYT/Portland Press Herald/Siena poll has Collins at 49% and Jackson at 46%, with a margin of error of about ±4.9. Newsweek reported this as Collins's first lead over Jackson in an independent poll.

A UNH Survey Center poll released 9/24/2026 has Jackson at 51% and Collins at 47%, which UNH calls a statistical tie, largely unchanged since July. Independents split 49% Jackson, 47% Collins. Collins's favorability among likely voters is 37% favorable, 51% unfavorable.

A Wedgewood poll dated Oct 1 shows Jackson 52%, Collins 48%. The Pollsmax polling average has Jackson ahead 49.5% to 46.5%. These figures come from a search-result summary, not a full read of the page.

Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary but withdrew on July 10 after a sexual assault allegation, which he denies. On July 25 a Democratic convention in Bangor nominated former state Senate president Troy Jackson, who beat Saundra Pelletier 566 votes to 5.
Jackson is the first replacement U.S. Senate nominee in Maine since 1918. He is now the Democratic nominee for resolution purposes, and Collins is the Republican nominee.

Maine's general election uses ranked-choice voting, so if no one wins a first-round majority, the result can depend on later-round tabulation. The race resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call it, or otherwise on official certification.
The general election is on November 3, 2026, and the question closes on November 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC.

In 2020 Collins beat Democrat Sara Gideon by about 9 points even though pre-election polls showed her losing, and Biden carried Maine by about 9 points on the same ballot. Collins has also won the 1996, 2002, 2008 and 2014 Senate races, making 5 of 5 overall. That count is recalled from memory and unverified here.

In the Siena poll of 619 registered voters, majorities want Democrats to control the Senate. Collins still leads on bringing resources to Maine, and Jackson's favorability is slightly underwater, which the article links to pro-Collins spending.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Unnamed people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the East-West pipeline is still running normally after reports of a new weekend strike on a pumping station near Khurais. Saudi Aramco and the Energy Ministry did not immediately answer Bloomberg's requests for comment. The 'operating normally' claim comes from those sources, not from the government.

Reports say that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Aramco has said anything publicly about the pipeline since it was attacked in September. Every report of a restart or higher flows so far comes from anonymous sources or market-intelligence firms.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia raised flows on the 7 million b/d East-West pipeline to more than 80% of capacity, close to 6 million b/d, with about 4.5 million b/d available for export. These figures came from tanker-tracking and market data such as Kepler, not from a government statement.

Anonymous Reuters sources said the pipeline restarted on September 22 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million b/d. The article cites no statement from the government or the Ministry of Energy.

The Ministry of Energy said in an official SPA statement that the East-West pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after several drone attacks on September 10 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The ministry said teams were taking steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.
The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, carried out by several drones from Iraq, saying it caused injuries and 'some damage that is currently being addressed.'

Precedent from earlier in 2026: after attacks in April cut flows on the East-West pipeline, the Ministry of Energy announced through SPA on April 12 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has publicly confirmed restorations before. This is a single case.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the closure would be a short interruption lasting days. He is a US official, not part of the Saudi government, so his statement does not count toward resolution.

Sources gave different repair estimates: one said five to six weeks, another said sooner. After the September 22 restart, Reuters sources said getting back to full capacity would likely take at least six to eight weeks.

The question resolves Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is currently operating, at any capacity, by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Anonymous-source reports like the Reuters and Bloomberg pieces do not count, and neither do statements about future or planned resumption. Based on what was found, no qualifying government statement has been reported as of October 5.

About 26 days remain before the deadline (October 31, 11:59 PM ET; the question closes November 1, 03:59 UTC). No scheduled ministry briefing on the pipeline was found. Attacks are continuing, including the reported strike near Khurais on the weekend of October 3–4.

market.question: Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement announced by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a ceasefire agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify. Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement. Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g. restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

All listed countries/parties must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for a Yes resolution. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a ceasefire agreement will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where a potentially qualifying announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a ceasefire agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries/parties or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 7 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the seventh calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, the announcements will be judged based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia and Houthi leadership; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?

CRTA's campaign monitoring reports that the Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, has had no live appearances on national TV since the list was declared on September 15. Over the same period Vučić made 17 appearances, in which he portrayed the Student List as 'anti-Serbian' and acting on 'orders from abroad'. market.question: Will Saudi airspace be closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Saudi Arabian Airspace (The Jeddah Flight Information Region (FIR)/OEJD) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before market creation; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before market creation, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Saudi Arabian government, including the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), and Saudi Air Navigation Services (SANS), and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 31?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Unnamed people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the East-West pipeline is still running normally after reports of a new weekend strike on a pumping station near Khurais. Saudi Aramco and the Energy Ministry did not immediately answer Bloomberg's requests for comment. The 'operating normally' claim comes from those sources, not from the government.

Reports say that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Aramco has said anything publicly about the pipeline since it was attacked in September. Every report of a restart or higher flows so far comes from anonymous sources or market-intelligence firms.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia raised flows on the 7 million b/d East-West pipeline to more than 80% of capacity, close to 6 million b/d, with about 4.5 million b/d available for export. These figures came from tanker-tracking and market data such as Kepler, not from a government statement.

Anonymous Reuters sources said the pipeline restarted on September 22 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million b/d. The article cites no statement from the government or the Ministry of Energy.

The Ministry of Energy said in an official SPA statement that the East-West pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after several drone attacks on September 10 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The ministry said teams were taking steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.
The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, carried out by several drones from Iraq, saying it caused injuries and 'some damage that is currently being addressed.'

Precedent from earlier in 2026: after attacks in April cut flows on the East-West pipeline, the Ministry of Energy announced through SPA on April 12 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has publicly confirmed restorations before. This is a single case.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the closure would be a short interruption lasting days. He is a US official, not part of the Saudi government, so his statement does not count toward resolution.

Sources gave different repair estimates: one said five to six weeks, another said sooner. After the September 22 restart, Reuters sources said getting back to full capacity would likely take at least six to eight weeks.

The question resolves Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is currently operating, at any capacity, by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Anonymous-source reports like the Reuters and Bloomberg pieces do not count, and neither do statements about future or planned resumption. Based on what was found, no qualifying government statement has been reported as of October 5.

About 26 days remain before the deadline (October 31, 11:59 PM ET; the question closes November 1, 03:59 UTC). No scheduled ministry briefing on the pipeline was found. Attacks are continuing, including the reported strike near Khurais on the weekend of October 3–4.

recent_facts.fact: Yahoo's live blog says the Rays beat the Yankees in Game 2 at Tropicana Field on Oct 5 and lead the best-of-five ALDS 2-0, so New York must win Games 3, 4 and 5. I could not find a confirmed final score. One search summary gave 7-5, but that figure appears to come from the 2020 Rays-Yankees series, so it is unverified.

In Game 2, Freddy Peralta retired the first 9 Yankees and allowed 1 run in 4 2/3 innings. Ben Rice tied it 1-1 with a 4th-inning homer, which was New York's first hit, but Tampa Bay went up 3-1 in the 5th. Cam Schlittler gave up 3 runs in 4 1/3 innings.

The Yankees made three defensive miscues in the first inning of Game 2: a McMahon error, a wild throw by Jazz Chisholm Jr. that let a run score, and catcher's interference on Austin Wells. That put Tampa Bay up 1-0 and pushed Schlittler to 19 pitches in the inning.

The Rays won Game 1 1-0 at Tropicana Field on Oct 3. Drew Rasmussen took a no-hitter into the 8th inning with 10 strikeouts and 2 walks before Austin Wells doubled with two outs. Jonathan Aranda's 3rd-inning homer off Gerrit Cole was the only run.
Remaining schedule: Game 3 at Yankee Stadium on Oct 7, Game 4 at Yankee Stadium on Oct 8 if needed, and Game 5 at Tampa Bay on Oct 10 if needed.

10 MLB teams have come back from 0-2 down to win a best-of-five series, about 11% of roughly 90 such series. The comebacks include the 2001 Yankees over Oakland and the 2017 Yankees over Cleveland, and the most recent was 2017. I could not confirm how many 0-2 series have been played since then (the total may now be above 90), so treat the exact rate as unverified.

The projected Game 3 Yankees starter was Carlos Rodón (tentative), who threw eight scoreless innings against Tampa Bay on Sept 22. The Rays listed Nick Martinez or Freddy Peralta for Game 3, but Peralta has now started Game 2.

Rasmussen went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA and an AL-best 0.91 WHIP, and has a career 1.81 ERA against the Yankees. Peralta was the AL Pitcher of the Month for September, going 5-0 with a 0.79 ERA over his last six starts. Schlittler finished with a 1.95 ERA, and Cole had a 2.50 ERA in three starts against Tampa Bay this season.

market.question: Will the rate of CPI inflation be above 3.6% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 3.6%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 3.6% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the
government shutdown

recent_facts.fact: BLS plans to release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA's weekly national average gasoline price rose through September 2026: $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and $4.48 on Sept 24. AAA called Sept 24 the highest ever for that time of year. On Sept 17 it was more than $1 above a year earlier.

AAA said the September 2026 monthly average was a record for the month at $4.33, 50 cents above the previous September record. It blamed Strait of Hormuz volatility and high crude prices. By October 1 the average had dropped nearly 7 cents to $4.41, and it was $4.365 on October 5.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). One search summary put the August monthly average at $4.19, which doesn't fit with these weekly figures, so that number is unverified.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, up from 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3% after 0.2% in July. The gasoline index rose 3.9% in August, more than a third of the monthly all-items increase. Annual inflation stayed at 3.4%, the same as July.

The headline 12-month change BLS reports is calculated from not seasonally adjusted index levels and rounded to one decimal. So the September 12-month figure depends on the unadjusted August-to-September change, not the seasonally adjusted monthly figure.

recent_facts.fact: Only the result after 90 minutes plus stoppage time counts. A draw or a Canada win resolves No, and it is a friendly, so there is no extra time.

The USMNT host Canada in a friendly on October 6, 2026 at 8pm ET at Allianz Field in St. Paul, Minnesota. It is a US home venue, not a neutral ground, and it is the last match of the window before the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals in November.

The USMNT have won all three friendlies since the World Cup: 4-1 over Peru (Sept 26), 4-2 over Chile (Sept 29) and 3-0 over Mexico (Oct 3). That is 11-3 on aggregate. Their World Cup ended with a 4-1 loss to Belgium in the Round of 16 on July 6.

Canada have won both matches this window, 1-0 over Chile and 2-0 over Peru in Montreal on Oct 3. Against Peru they outshot their opponent 17-4, with xG of 1.94 to 0.23 and Jacob Shaffelburg scoring twice.
U.S. Soccer gives the all-time record as USA 17 wins, 12 losses and 13 draws against Canada. A 2025 U.S. Soccer preview cited elsewhere gives 20-14-11, so the sources disagree (unverified).

Canada won the last two meetings, both 2-1: a friendly in Kansas City on Sept 7, 2024 and the Nations League third-place match on March 23, 2025. The two teams have not played each other in 2026. This is a small sample.
The 2-1 loss in Kansas City in September 2024 was the first US home defeat to Canada in 67 years. Canada's previous win on US soil was 3-2 in St. Louis in 1957.

Canada's listed absences include Alphonso Davies, Alistair Johnston, Ismaël Koné, Moïse Bombito, Jonathan Osorio, Kamal Miller, Derek Cornelius, Ali Ahmed, Jayden Nelson and Maxime Crépeau. Tajon Buchanan and Cyle Larin left camp injured.

Pochettino started a very experienced team against Mexico, apart from teenagers Julian Hall and Cavan Sullivan, who both scored. He is reported to be planning more rotation against Canada, with Sergino Dest, George Campbell and Neil Pierre in line for minutes in defense.

At the 2026 World Cup, Canada drew 1-1 with Bosnia and Herzegovina, beat Qatar 6-0 and lost 2-1 to Switzerland, finishing second in Group D. They then beat South Africa 1-0 and were knocked out by Morocco. Earlier in 2026 they drew with Iceland, Tunisia and Ireland and beat Uzbekistan 2-0.

US results in 2026 before the World Cup were mixed: they lost 5-2 to Belgium and 2-0 to Portugal, beat Senegal 3-2 and lost 2-1 to Germany. At the World Cup they went 3 wins and 2 losses (4-1 Paraguay, 2-0 Australia, 2-3 Türkiye, 2-0 Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1-4 Belgium).

recent_facts.fact: No. 2 Georgia (5-0, 3-0 SEC) plays No. 6 Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC) on Saturday, Oct 10, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC. The game is at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, so Alabama is the true home team. Both markets resolve on the official final result. College football has overtime, so the game cannot end in a tie.

Georgia is 2-14 in games played in Tuscaloosa. Its last win there was 26-23 in overtime on Sept 22, 2007, which SI/Hot Augusta also report. Alabama won the last two Tuscaloosa meetings: 41-24 in 2020 and 41-34 in 2024.

Alabama leads the all-time series 45-27-4. Alabama won 7 of the last 10 meetings and Georgia won 3. The two most recent: Alabama won 24-21 in Athens on Sept 27, 2025, and Georgia won 28-7 in the SEC Championship in Atlanta on Dec 6, 2025. This is a small sample covering different venues and coaching eras.

Alabama is 5-0 after beating Mississippi State 56-23 on the road on Oct 3. Its earlier results: 48-10 vs East Carolina, 45-17 at Kentucky, 50-36 vs Florida State and 49-18 vs South Carolina. That is 248 points scored and 104 allowed.

Georgia is 5-0: 63-3 vs Tennessee State (FCS), 70-20 vs Western Kentucky, 45-17 at Arkansas, 41-13 vs Oklahoma and 38-14 vs Vanderbilt. That is 257 points scored and 67 allowed. Wikipedia lists Alabama as Georgia's first ranked opponent of the season.

In the 38-14 win over Vanderbilt, Georgia QB Gunner Stockton went 25 of 32 for a season-high 295 yards and 3 TDs. Georgia ran for 176 yards on 34 carries and held Vanderbilt to 293 total yards, 61 of them in the second half. Vanderbilt was playing its backup QB.
Gunner Stockton, a fifth-year player, has started all five Georgia games. Wikipedia reports no significant Georgia injuries through Week 5.

Before the Mississippi State game, Kalen DeBoer said right tackle Jayvin James was questionable with a lower-extremity injury from the South Carolina game. He also said William Sanders had an upper-body injury and was expected to play. Linebackers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu were out, with Umeozulu out longer. Reports describe Alabama's offensive line as banged up. No status update for Georgia week was found.
President Trump announced he will attend the game in Tuscaloosa. It is the third straight year the two teams meet in the regular season.

recent_facts.fact: Bears starting QB Caleb Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury with a reported 3-4 week timeline. He has missed two straight games (Weeks 3 and 4), and reports call him likely out for the Week 5 game at Green Bay. Date approximate: reports published before the Oct 4 Jets game.

Williams is described as week-to-week and had not been officially ruled out for Week 5. Case Keenum started and won the Week 3 game 27-7 over Philadelphia, and Bagent started the Week 4 win over the Jets. That makes the Bears 2-0 with backup QBs this season.

Head coach Matt LaFleur said Packers LB Edgerrin Cooper is expected to miss the rest of the season with an apparent Achilles tear from the Bucs game, pending an MRI. Isaiah McDuffie is expected to start alongside Zaire Franklin.

Against Tampa Bay, Packers CB Brandon Cisse hurt his neck and was evaluated for a concussion. RB Chris Brooks and DT Devonte Wyatt left in the first half with ankle injuries, and McDuffie briefly left with an eye injury. Edge rusher Micah Parsons is still out recovering from ACL surgery after tearing it in December 2025.

The Packers lead the all-time series 109-98-6 over 213 meetings, and the Bears lead 2-1 in the playoffs. The Bears have won the last 2 meetings: 22-16 on Dec 20, 2025 and 31-27 in the Jan 10, 2026 Wild Card game.

In the 10 meetings that page lists (Sep 2018 to Jan 2026), the Packers won 6 and the Bears won 4. The Bears' last win at Lambeau was 24-22 on Jan 5, 2025. The list appears incomplete: by unverified recall it leaves out the 2023 games and a Dec 7, 2025 Packers win at Lambeau, possibly 28-21. Treat it as a small, unverified sample.
There is no 2026 regular-season head-to-head yet. This Oct 11 game is the first of the two scheduled division meetings.

recent_facts.fact: Croatia host Spain at Stadion Poljud in Split on October 6, 2026 (7:45 PM UK time) in UEFA Nations League League A Group 3. Erik Lambrechts is the referee, per 101GreatGoals.

Spain top the group with 3 wins from 3 (9 pts): 3-2 at England (Sep 26), 4-1 vs Croatia (Sep 29) and 3-1 vs Czechia (Oct 3). Croatia are 3rd with 3 pts after beating Czechia 2-1 (Sep 26), losing 1-4 to Spain and losing 0-7 to England.
Croatia lost 7-0 at home to England on October 3, 2026, and were 4-0 down at halftime. Kane and Saka scored twice each, with Bellingham, Gordon and Rogers adding one apiece.
Croatia coach Slaven Bilić called the 7-0 loss to England 'a nightmare of a night' and 'the heaviest defeat in our history', and said it was not a true reflection of his team.
Spain beat Croatia 4-1 in Seville on September 29, 2026, with Lamine Yamal scoring twice. That game was the reverse of this week's fixture.
Spain beat Czechia 3-1 in Oviedo on October 3 with goals from Yamal, Rodri and Merino, extending their unbeaten run to 41 matches in all competitions. Czechia had Krejčí sent off late in the game.

Spain made nine changes against Czechia. Yamal and Baena were taken off at halftime for tactical reasons. Ferran Torres, Nico Williams and Alex Grimaldo had already withdrawn from the squad, and Cubarsí sat out to recover.

Croatia picked up no significant new injuries against England. Their expected XI includes Livaković, Gvardiol, Modrić, Kovačić and Vlašić, and Spain have no fresh injury concerns. Vušković, Pašalić, Mišić, Sučić and Pongračić are one booking from a suspension.

market.question: Will average **gas prices** be above $4.00? (Above 4.00)
market.rules: If average regular gas prices for the United States are strictly greater than $4.00 on Nov 3, 2026 according to AAA, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.fact: AAA's national average for regular gas was $4.3653 on Oct 5, 2026. It was $4.3697 the day before, $4.4768 a week earlier, $4.1459 a month earlier and $3.1339 a year earlier. The average sits about 11.5 cents above the $4.25 threshold.

On Oct 1 the national average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents from $4.48 a week earlier. WTI settled at $90.42, EIA gasoline demand fell to 8.68 million barrels a day, and U.S. crude stocks rose 0.9 million barrels to 427.3 million.

September 2026 averaged $4.33 a gallon, a record for the month and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023. AAA said prices were the highest they had ever been for this time of year.
Gasoline futures fell 1.8% to $3.25 a gallon on Oct 5, 2026. Crude oil fell 0.53% to $90.62 a barrel, which is down 2.59% over the past month but 46.9% higher than a year ago.

Crude oil fell to about $90 a barrel on Oct 5 as signs of more global supply outweighed Middle East risks. The previous Friday, G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves.

Georgia has a 30-day suspension of its 33.3-cent gas tax that runs through Oct 29, and its prices are down 34–38 cents. Ohio announced a 90-day suspension on Sept 30 that runs to the end of the year, and its prices are down 39–43 cents.

Indiana suspended its state gas tax and has the nation's lowest prices at $3.74. Kentucky and Illinois cut or paused tax increases, and California and Michigan allowed early use of winter-blend gasoline. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan called the decline 'not exactly the most organic' because refineries behind the Strait of Hormuz still cannot fully move their products.
Georgia's gas tax holiday is due to end Oct 29, five days before the Nov 3 resolution date, unless it is extended again. Ohio's suspension runs past Nov 3.

Crude moving through Hormuz reached a 7-day average of 13.5 million barrels a day, back to the prewar level and up from about 6–8 million in mid-September. Refined product shipments were only 677,000 barrels a day, against 3.6 million before the war.

Foreign Policy reported that oil is flowing out of the Strait of Hormuz again, but refinery damage and disrupted shipping are expected to keep gasoline and diesel prices high. Tanker freight rates have risen about twentyfold since the war began.

GasBuddy's pre-war seasonal pattern for 2026 had prices falling through the fall to a yearly low in December. This reflects the usual autumn decline after the switch to winter-blend gasoline, which typically happens in mid-September.
AAA updates its national average for regular gasoline daily, quoted to four decimal places. The question resolves Yes only if the Nov 3, 2026 figure is strictly greater than $4.25.

Positive comments without explicit support, policy endorsements without nominee endorsement, or conditional endorsements do not qualify. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 3, 2026, the US naval blockade of Iran was still in force, and Trump was sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Diplomacy was reported as deadlocked.

Preliminary tanker-tracking estimates showed Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first such month since the war began in February.

Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal, under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade, removed oil sanctions and reinstated a regional ceasefire. Trump said Iran had 'overplayed their hand' but said he expected talks to resume that week.

On October 4, Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran was still reviewing a US counterproposal, sent through intermediaries. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said it was 'in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues.' FM Araghchi said there is 'no military solution.'

The two sides disagree on what comes first. Iran insists the Hormuz and US blockade issues be settled first, while Washington insists on nuclear concessions. Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive the talks.

Trump said he was 'open to a deal, but not to the one the Iranians offered.' He reportedly told officials he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. The US also launched an expanded sanctions regime, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' in August 2026.

An IRGC advisor claimed that no US naval vessels are now in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman, and that US warships have pulled back 1,000 km. This is an Iranian claim; no official US announcement about the blockade accompanied it.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June MOU, including ending the naval blockade. Araghchi said the strait could reopen within seven days if those conditions are met.

Precedent: the first blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026 (about 66 days). On June 14 Trump said he had 'authorized lifting the US naval blockade' once an accord was reached. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18. That is one prior instance, so this is an unverified base rate.
The second blockade phase began July 14–15, 2026, after Trump's July 13 announcement, and was about 83 days old as of October 5. More than 100 vessels had been redirected by September 12.

No signed agreement or scheduled formal US-Iran negotiating session was reported before October 31. The next known date is the US midterm election on November 3, after which Trump reportedly expects renewed bombing.

Only an official, unambiguous US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts. Iranian claims, leaks, partial exemptions for specific vessels, and naval repositioning without an announcement do not qualify.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%. That makes 4.00% the upper bound going into the October meeting. It was the first hike since July 2023 and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh.

The September dot plot had a median of 4.1% for end-2026, which means one more 25 bp hike this year. 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026 and four projected two. The median showed no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028-2029.

The September statement cited persistent inflation, with core PCE above 3% in every month of 2026, and 'geopolitical developments'. Three members had already favored a hike at the July meeting. Only two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.
September nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August payrolls were revised down by a combined 60,000.

Before the jobs report, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said labor market conditions 'have stabilized'. NY Fed President John Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' in deciding whether to follow September's hike with another.

Before the jobs data, Williams called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that inflation expectations could become entrenched after five years above target. Governor Lisa Cook said AI appears to be adding inflationary pressure and that the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'.
At Jackson Hole in late August, Warsh said 'We have work to do' and suggested a rate hike in the coming months because of high inflation.

After the September jobs report, coverage shifted toward the Fed skipping October and possibly hiking in December. J.P. Morgan's stated base case is one more hike at the December meeting, and it notes that one argument for skipping October is giving the September hike time to work.
The September 2026 CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the main inflation release still to come before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

facts_dropped.fact: At his September press conference Warsh said 'Inflation is too high and has been for too long.' He said the hike was made because the committee was not confident that underlying inflation was moving toward 2% fast enough. Warsh did not submit SEP projections because he views them as forward guidance.
