market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: The MK the President picks to form a government gets 28 days, and the President can extend that by up to 14 more days (42 days at most). If that MK fails, the President can give a second MK 28 days with no extension. The question counts only a PM who is formally sworn in, and it closes on 2026-10-28, one day after the vote.

Election day for all 120 Knesset seats is October 27, 2026. Surplus-vote agreements are due October 16, diplomatic voting is October 20, and official results are certified November 4, 2026. 61 seats make a majority.

Unverified recall: after the Nov 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu's government was sworn in on Dec 29, 2022, about 58 days later. After the March 23, 2021 election, Bennett's government was sworn in on June 13, 2021. The April 2019 and September 2019 elections produced no government.

Netanyahu leads the outgoing 37th government. The 25th Knesset dissolved on its scheduled date, July 17, 2026, after serving its full four-year term. Likud is running merged with New Hope, and Bennett and Lapid are running together on the 'Together' list.

market.question: Will CPI Core rise more than 0.1% in September? (Above 0.1%)
market.rules:
If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for September 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.1%, then the market resolves to Yes.
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: Seasonally adjusted core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month in August 2026. The 12-month core rate was 2.4%, the lowest since March 2021.

Recent monthly core CPI changes: April 2026 +0.4%, May +0.2%, June +0.0%, July +0.2%, August +0.3%. That means 4 of the last 5 months were above 0.1%, and June (0.0%) was the only one at or below 0.1%.
Shelter, the largest part of core CPI, rose 0.3% in August 2026 after two straight monthly gains of 0.1% (June and July). Shelter was up 3.0% year over year.
Headline CPI rose 0.4% in August 2026, and annual inflation was 3.4%. Gasoline rose 3.9% in the month and was up 27.4% year over year. Energy is pushing headline inflation well above the core rate.

recent_facts.source: BLS Schedule of Selected Releases 2026 / USInflationCalculator
recent_facts.fact: BLS is scheduled to publish the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. That is after the question's close time of 12:25 UTC (8:25 a.m. ET) the same day.

Congress passed a continuing resolution (House vote 370-48) that funds the government through December 11, 2026. This avoided a shutdown on October 1, 2026, so a shutdown delay to the September CPI release is not expected.

The question uses the one-decimal, seasonally adjusted month-over-month change in CPI-U all items less food and energy, as published by BLS. A published 0.1% or lower resolves No, and 0.2% or higher resolves Yes. For reference, August's unrounded core change was about 0.29%, which BLS published as 0.3%.

During the October 1 to November 12, 2025 shutdown, BLS canceled the October 2025 CPI report and released the November report late, on December 18. This is the only recent case of a shutdown affecting CPI publication.

market.question: NATO x Russia military clash by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between market creation and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Nov 1, 2026? (Before Nov 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

market.question: Will Bernie Sanders endorse James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026?
market.rules:
If Bernie Sanders publicly endorses James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
An endorsement requires a clear, affirmative statement of support for the nominee's election. The statement must be public (not private communications) and specifically reference the race or be clearly in context of the race. The endorsement must come directly from the person or through their official channels. Positive comments without explicit support, policy endorsements without nominee endorsement, or conditional endorsements do not qualify. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. Sarcastic statements or those immediately clarified as jokes do not qualify.

An announcement, threat, or claim that the Houthis have lost control will not qualify without actual control being established.

If control changes pursuant to a negotiated settlement, ceasefire term, surrender, or transfer agreement, this will qualify only once actual control has been established on the island.

market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 15?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $80 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

WTI settled at $91.11 on Friday, October 2, down $1.76 from Thursday's $92.87 settlement. The drop followed a European agreement to release emergency diesel stocks under a G7/IEA plan of about 100 million barrels.
On October 1, WTI jumped nearly 3% to $92.87 after a U.S. aircraft carrier deployment. EnergyNow also cited China's suspension of fuel exports and renewed U.S.-Iran military concerns that day.

Oil fell on October 5 as Middle East crude exports rose and the G7 released about 100 million barrels of reserves. Higher loadings through the Strait of Hormuz and continued operation of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline eased supply concerns. Brent was about $102.40 and WTI about $90.65.

Saudi Aramco cut its November Arab Light price to Asia to $5 below the regional benchmark as Middle Eastern flows normalize. Saudi-backed forces in Yemen launched operations against Houthi areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and OPEC+ kept quotas unchanged.
WTI closed at $96.05 on September 9, 2026, its highest close since May 22. Oil rose more than 8% in September as the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes.

Recent swings were large. WTI closed at $82.49 on Jul 17 and $92.19 on Jul 23 (+6% that day on Red Sea tanker attacks), then $82.61 on Jul 27 (-7.5%). It fell from $96.02 on Jun 3 to $69.63 on Jun 24.

On September 8, oil rose to $99 (headline figure, likely Brent) on a report that Iran launched a second undisclosed attack on U.S. Navy ships. WTI's highest close since late May was $96.05, so WTI has not been confirmed above $100 since May.

market.question: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 0bps at their October 2026 meeting? (Fed maintains rate)
market.rules:
If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of 0bps on October 28, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The outcomes are mutually exclusive: at most one can resolve to Yes. For example, a 50-basis-point hike resolves “Hike   25 bps” to Yes and “Hike 25 bps” to No.

If the scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, “Fed maintains rate” resolves to Yes and all other outcomes resolve to No.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the Fed's first rate hike since 2023.

recent_facts.source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (FOMC statement summary)
recent_facts.fact: The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at about 4.1%. It shows no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028–2029. Four participants projected two more hikes in 2026. Only the October 28 and December meetings remain this year.

September nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000–100,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%. Jefferies' chief U.S. economist called the report 'the nail in the coffin for an October hike'.

New York Fed President John Williams, a permanent FOMC voter, said: 'With the policy action we took at our September meeting, there is no need for urgency.' He added that incoming data 'should provide greater clarity'. Earlier, on Sept 24, he had called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said, 'I don't currently see an urgent need for further action.' She wants time to judge the effects of the September hike. Bowman has indicated she prefers no further hikes in 2026.
After the jobs report, coverage said at least three FOMC voters were in no rush for another hike. Expectations for the next move shifted toward the December meeting rather than October 27–28.

Before the jobs report, several officials sounded hawkish. Governor Lisa Cook said the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'. Barr (Sept 23) said further adjustments were likely needed, and Hammack (Sept 25) worried about inflation expectations. Paulson (Sept 24) said more increases may be needed.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'inflation is too high and has been for too long'. He estimated that PCE inflation was running at 3.6% year over year through August. Three members had dissented at the prior (July) meeting in favor of a hike.

August 2026 CPI rose 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year. Core CPI rose 0.3% month over month and 2.4% year over year, down from 2.5%. Gasoline, up 3.9% on the month, accounted for over a third of the monthly increase.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. That is the main inflation report due before the October meeting.

The FOMC meets October 27–28, 2026, and the decision is announced Wednesday, October 28. That is days before the November midterm elections. The minutes of the September meeting are also due in October.

These outcomes are mutually exclusive. 'Fed maintains rate' resolves Yes if the 3.75%–4.00% target range is unchanged on October 28, or if the meeting is canceled. 'Hike 25bps' resolves Yes only on an increase of exactly 25 bps.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić be the next Prime Minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: An early parliamentary election for all 250 National Assembly seats is set for 25 October 2026, after Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 September. Seats are allocated by closed-list PR with d'Hondt and a 3% threshold, which is waived for minority parties. A majority is 126 seats.

Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist and medical professor born in 1970, heads the ballot for the 'Student List – Students Are Winning' in the 2026 election. Reporting describes him as the Student List's lead candidate for prime minister.
Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister. He heads SNS's 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list.

Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister on 3 October at Belgrade Arena and promised a 'comprehensive' victory. Al Jazeera reports that if SNS wins a majority, parliament would elect Vučić as PM. It describes the Student List as the main challenger.
A Faktor Plus poll had Vučić's United Serbia at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%. That was a 5.6-point gain for the Student List.
An NSPM poll presented by Vukadinović had the Student List at 44.4% and United Serbia at 41.7%. The exact publication date is approximate: late September or early October 2026.
Speaking from New York, Vučić was reported as saying the Student List leads and is 'hard to catch'.
Another poll had the Student List at 39.6% and SNS at 37.5%. Wikipedia sums up recent polling as a tightened race in which results vary by pollster.

Other lists include European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš), Authentic Right (Miloš Jovanović) and the SPS-led Factor of Stability (Ivica Dačić). SSP said it would cooperate with the Student List. PSG dropped out of the race to back the Student List.
Election day is 25 October 2026, the same day this question closes. A PM can only be elected later, after the new Assembly holds its constitutive session.

After the 17 December 2023 election, the new Assembly first met on 6 February 2024 and the President named Vučević PM-designate on 30 March. The government was elected on 2 May 2024, about 4.5 months after the vote, with 152 votes in favour.

Under Serbian procedure, the President gives the mandate to a PM-designate, and the Assembly then elects the PM and cabinet by a majority of all 250 MPs, meaning 126 votes. Vučić has resigned, so who will give the mandate after the vote is not confirmed in these sources (unverified).

market.question: Will Bitcoin be above $100000 by November 1, 2026 at 12:00AM ET? (Before November 2026)
market.rules:
If the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $100000.00 starting Jul 21, 2026 and before Nov 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

market.question: Argentina vs. Benin: Both Teams to Score
market.rules:

This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Argentina and Benin each score at least one goal during the game.

This market will resolve to "No" if either team fails to score (i.e., if one or both teams finish with zero goals).

If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed. If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50–50.

If the game is started but not completed, this market will resolve according to the official final score published on fifa.com. This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

recent_facts.fact: Resolves Yes only if Argentina and Benin each score at least once within 90 minutes plus stoppage time. If either side finishes with zero goals it resolves No, so a 0-0 draw or any shutout win is No.

Argentina host Benin in a friendly on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 at 20:00 local time at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Argentina are the true home side. The match is Lionel Messi's farewell game for the national team.

This will be Messi's 208th cap. He leaves as Argentina's all-time top scorer with 125 goals. About 85,000 fans are expected at a sold-out ground, and 2022 World Cup winners have been invited to the celebrations. Benin were picked partly because European teams had Nations League games and partly because their match fee was lower.

Scaloni's expected lineup is close to a first-choice XI: E. Martínez; Giay, Romero, Otamendi, Tagliafico; De Paul, Enzo Fernández, Mac Allister; Messi, Julián Álvarez, Lautaro Martínez. This is a projected lineup, not a confirmed one.
Benin beat Mauritania 2-1 on September 29 in Abidjan in AFCON 2027 qualifying, with Rodolfo Aloko scoring both goals (31' and 46'). Benin lead Group F on 4 points.
Benin drew 1-1 away to Burkina Faso on September 25, 2026 in their first AFCON 2027 qualifier.

Goal lists Benin's last five results as W 2-1 Mauritania, D 1-1 Burkina Faso, D 1-1 Niger, L 1-5 Togo, W 1-0 Guinea. That is 6 scored and 8 conceded, with Benin scoring in all five. Goal also lists Argentina wins of 7-0 over Burkina Faso (Oct 4) and 4-0 over Bolivia (Oct 1), but no other source I found confirms these, and they look doubtful because Benin played Burkina Faso in that window.
Benin's captain and striker Steve Mounié is out of Gernot Rohr's 25-man squad for this window through injury. The squad has 8 forwards, including first-time call-up Joseph Ede Oloko.

Argentina's reported 2026 World Cup results: 3-0 Algeria, 2-0 Austria, 3-1 Jordan, 3-2 Egypt, 3-1 Switzerland (after extra time), 2-1 England, and a 0-1 loss to Spain after extra time. That is 2 clean sheets in 7 games, and they conceded in 5. The Round of 32 result was not in the summary I found.
Argentina lost the World Cup final 1-0 to Spain on a 106th-minute Ferran Torres goal. Enzo Fernández was sent off and Argentina did not take a single shot in regulation time.
This is the first-ever meeting between Argentina and Benin, so there is no head-to-head record.

From memory, not checked against a source: Argentina's recent friendlies against weaker teams have often ended in shutouts, e.g. 2023 Panama 2-0 and Curaçao 7-0, 2024 El Salvador 3-0 and Ecuador 1-0, 2025 Angola 2-0 and Puerto Rico 6-0. market.question: Will CPI rise more than 0.5% in September 2026? (Above 0.5%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% (single-decimal) in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will always close at 8:25 AM ET on the scheduled day of the data release (October 14, 2026). Please note: the Expiration Value is the single-decimal value published at the Source Agency. In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August 2026, after 0.1% in July. Over 12 months, all items rose 3.4% before seasonal adjustment.

In August 2026 (seasonally adjusted), gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the all-items increase. Energy rose 2.1%, food 0.1%, shelter 0.3% and core (less food and energy) 0.3%, up from 0.2% in July.

Seasonally adjusted monthly all-items CPI changes in 2026: Feb +0.3%, Mar +0.9%, Apr +0.6%, May +0.5%, Jun -0.4%, Jul +0.1%, Aug +0.4%. That is 2 of 7 months above 0.5%, 3 of 7 above 0.4%, and 1 of 7 above 0.6%.

AAA's September 2026 average for regular gasoline was $4.33 a gallon, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). On Oct 1 the national average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents on the week, with crude back in the $90 per barrel range.

The August 2026 national average gas price was $4.19 a gallon, using EIA data. This is a different provider from AAA, so comparing it with AAA's $4.33 September average (roughly +3%) is only approximate.

AAA's weekly national averages in September 2026: $4.14 (Sep 3), $4.27 (Sep 10), $4.43 (Sep 17), $4.48 (Sep 24). AAA said $4.48 was the highest ever for that time of year, driven by volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude prices.
August 2026 was the most expensive August ever at the pump, with the national average above $4 every day of the month. The previous August record average was $3.97 (2022).

Gasoline CPI was up 27.4% year over year in August 2026, and core CPI was up 2.4% year over year. Gas prices had been $2.98 a gallon on Feb 28, 2026, before U.S. military operations against Iran began.
BLS is scheduled to publish the September 2026 CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.

The headline figure is the seasonally adjusted one-month percent change in CPI-U, rounded to one decimal. For the seasonal factors introduced in January 2026, BLS used intervention-analysis seasonal adjustment on 57 series, including motor fuels.

Precedent: in the Oct 1 to Nov 12, 2025 shutdown (43 days), BLS pushed the September 2025 CPI back from Oct 15 to Oct 24 so Social Security could meet its COLA deadlines, and it cancelled the October 2025 CPI. My searches found no reporting of a 2026 shutdown affecting BLS (unverified).

market.question: Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 4.00% following the Fed's Oct 28, 2026 meeting? (Above 4.00%)
market.rules:
If the upper bound of the target federal funds rate published on the Federal Reserve's official website is greater than 4.00% following the Federal Reserve's Oct 28, 2026 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market will expire the first 2:05 PM ET following the release of a Federal Reserve statement for their Oct 28, 2026 meeting or one week following the last day of that meeting.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00%. This was the Fed's first rate increase since 2023, and it leaves the upper bound at exactly 4.00%.

The current upper bound is 4.00%, so the question needs a hike at the October 27-28 meeting to resolve Yes. A hold or a cut would leave the upper bound at or below 4.00%. A 25 bp hike would make the range 4.00%–4.25%.
New York Fed President John Williams said on Sept. 29 that one more rate increase by the end of this year could be appropriate, but that there was no need to rush.

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said on Oct. 1 that policymakers must carefully assess trends in the data and the outlook when adjusting policy, and that reaching a judgment could take more time. Chair Kevin Warsh has avoided signaling the near-term path of rates.
August core PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y, below the 0.3% m/m and 3.3% y/y consensus. Headline PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.4% y/y, with annual rates unchanged from revised July.

August CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y, in line with estimates, driven by a 3.9% jump in gasoline prices. Energy prices were up 16.3% y/y amid Middle East tensions. Core CPI rose 0.3% m/m. The search summary gave core CPI at 2.4% y/y, which looks inconsistent with core PCE at 3.0%, so that figure is unverified.

Speaking at Jackson Hole, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'we have work to do' on inflation and signaled a possible rate hike. At the September press conference he said inflation 'is too high, and has been for too long.'
Data still due before the Oct 28 decision: September CPI on Oct 14, September PPI on Oct 15, and import/export prices on Oct 16, all at 8:30 AM ET. The FOMC statement is due Oct 28 at 2:00 PM ET.

In late September, fixed-income traders saw the Oct. 28 meeting as the most likely point for the next move, which would take the range to 4.00%–4.25%. A Bloomingbit report on Oct 3 said expectations of an October hike fell quickly after Williams' remarks and the softer August PCE data.

facts_dropped.fact: In the September Summary of Economic Projections, the median participant showed one more 25 bp hike in 2026, ending the year at 4.1%. The median showed no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028 and 2029. Two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.

market.question: Will Bank of Canada Hike rates by 0bps at their October 2026 meeting? (Maintains rate)
market.rules: If the Bank of Canada does a Hike of 0bps at its Oct 28, 2026 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.fact: On September 2, 2026 the Governing Council unanimously held the policy rate at 2.25%. Its deliberations summary put CPI near 3% for several months, CPI excluding gasoline at 2.2%, core inflation around 2%, unemployment around 6.5% and Q2 growth at 3.3% annualized, and said the economy is still in excess supply.

The September hold at 2.25% was the Bank of Canada's seventh straight decision leaving the rate unchanged. The Bank also flagged stronger upside risks to inflation, citing the Middle East conflict and the breakdown in Canada–U.S. trade talks.

In a September 21 speech in Halifax, Governor Macklem said the Bank doesn't want to raise rates and restrain growth if inflation pressures are contained, 'nor do we want to be too slow to respond if inflationary pressures are becoming more persistent.' He also said that if oil stays near $100 a barrel, inflation would be expected to edge up in the coming months.

UBS Global Research changed its call to a 25bp hike in October and another in January. Manulife and Oxford Economics now call for hikes in October and December, and Bank of Nova Scotia also calls for an October hike. UBS projects September CPI at 3.3%.
After Macklem's speech, TD Economics still called for the Bank of Canada to stay on hold for the rest of 2026.

Capital Economics calls for two quarter-point hikes starting next year (2027), which would take the policy rate to 2.75%, and cites U.S. trade friction and slower population growth. Senior Deputy Governor Rogers said the policy rate is too blunt a tool for housing affordability.

August CPI rose 3.0% year over year, the same as July. The Bank's preferred core measures averaged 2.0% (trim 1.9%, median 2.0%), and CPI excluding gasoline rose 2.4% after 2.2% in July. Gasoline inflation eased to 22.8% from 25.7%, and rent rose to 2.8% from 2.5%.
Analysts said the August core measures still showed limited evidence that high energy prices were spreading into broader inflation.
Q3 GDP growth is estimated at 1.4–2% annualized, Q2 GDP was up 1.2% year over year, and business investment rose for the first time since Q4 2024.
Statistics Canada is due to release the September Labour Force Survey on October 9, 2026.

The Bank of Canada is due to publish its Business Outlook Survey and Canadian Survey of Consumer Expectations on October 19, 2026 at 11:30 ET. September CPI is reported to be due around October 19–20.
The target for the overnight rate is currently 2.25%. A hold resolves 'Maintains rate' (0bps) and a move to 2.50% resolves 'Hike 25bps'.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Reason reports the current House has 218 Republicans (plus 1 independent) and 214 Democrats. It says the Cook Political Report rates 16 Republican-held seats and 6 Democratic-held seats as Toss Ups.

A search summary of the Cook House ratings gave these counts: 185 Solid D, 12 Likely D, 11 Lean D, 22 Toss Up, 10 Lean R, 19 Likely R, 176 Solid R. That is 208 seats rated Solid, Likely or Lean D and 205 rated Solid, Likely or Lean R. The Cook page itself returned 403, so these counts were not checked directly.

This lower-tier site reported a Cook ratings shift of 15 House races in early October 2026, after which 17 Republican-held seats and 5 Democratic-held seats were rated Toss Up. The direction of the shift is not confirmed from this source.

A CBS News/YouGov poll found Democrats ahead of Republicans 54% to 44% on the generic congressional ballot. Reports say the Democratic gains in polling that began in early September were still continuing.

Mid-decade redistricting was meant to give Republicans 5 seats in Texas, 4 in Florida, 2 in Ohio and 1 each in Alabama, Louisiana, Missouri, North Carolina and Tennessee. Democrats aimed for 5 in California. After court rulings (Missouri map overturned, Utah gaining a Democratic-leaning seat), Reason puts Republicans' theoretical redistricting edge at 9 districts, down from 16.

The U.S. Supreme Court stopped Missouri from using its new GOP-drawn congressional map in the 2026 midterms. This followed the Missouri Supreme Court's unanimous ruling on September 3, 2026, which ordered the 2022 map used in November and sent the new map to a referendum.

On June 10, 2026, the Florida Supreme Court declined to block DeSantis's new congressional map, which is designed to give Republicans up to 4 more seats. The map will be used for the November 3, 2026 election while the underlying lawsuit continues.

NBC's June state-by-state redistricting count: Republican gains of TX 3-5, FL 4, AL 1, LA 1, TN 1, NC 1, MO 1 and OH 1-2; Democratic gains of CA 4-5 and UT 1. In total that is up to 16 GOP and up to 6 Democratic seats. The April Supreme Court Voting Rights Act decision allowed Southern states to eliminate majority-Black districts. The Missouri map was later blocked.
Virginia voters approved a Democratic redistricting amendment with about 51% yes, but the Supreme Court of Virginia struck it down 4-3. Virginia's existing map (6 D, 5 R) stays in place for 2026.
Since 1946, the president's party has lost an average of about 25 House seats in midterms. The average loss is 37 seats when the president's approval was below 50% and 14 seats when it was above 50%.

The president's party lost House seats in 18 of 20 midterms over the past 80 years (90%). The only gains came in 1998 (Clinton) and 2002 (G.W. Bush), when both presidents had approval above 60%. This count comes from search-result summaries and is unverified.

The general election for all 435 House seats is on November 3, 2026, and a majority is 218 seats. The questions close on 2026-11-04 at 04:59 UTC (11:59 PM ET on election night), before many close races will have been called.

Control goes to whichever party wins a majority of voting seats (218 of 435). Independents count toward a party only if they caucus or announce they will. If no party has a majority, the party of the first elected Speaker of the 120th Congress is treated as the controlling party, and the question may stay open until January 4.

facts_dropped.fact: As of October 5, 2026, the Silver Bulletin generic congressional ballot polling average showed Democrats ahead by 8.9 points. Another aggregator listed Democrats at 51.2% and Republicans at 43.3% (D+8), and a third had 49.3% to 41.9% (D+7.4).
facts_dropped.reason: cites a forecaster

market.question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

recent_facts.fact: Preliminary figures show 290 vessels transited Bab el-Mandeb in the week of 21–27 September 2026 (about 41 per day) and 264 in the week of 14–20 September (about 38 per day). The four-week average was 280 per week (about 40 per day). This is Lloyd's List's own count, not IMF PortWatch's.
Bab el-Mandeb transits are above the levels seen before the 2026 Middle East Gulf crisis but below the peak driven by tankers. Weekly transits averaged 316 in June 2026 and 257 in January 2026.

recent_facts.source: USNI News / Al Jazeera (summarized via search)
recent_facts.fact: After the Houthis took Mokha, Perim Island and the rest of Yemen's Red Sea coast in September 2026, daily Bab el-Mandeb traffic fell from about 35 transits to 25. It then recovered and reached 45 transits on a Sunday.

Owners and operators are carrying out plans to return to the Red Sea, with ships that had avoided the route for years increasingly tracked sailing through it. The Houthi blockade of Saudi Arabia has dampened growth, but their threats have not derailed the return.

The Houthis now control Yemen's entire Red Sea coastline, including the Bab el-Mandeb approaches. They have declared a blockade on Saudi-flagged vessels and attacked energy infrastructure. Analysts note that shipping firms might avoid the strait based on perceived risk alone.
In September 2026 the Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline. Their stated maritime blockade targets Saudi Arabia, and they say other ships are free to pass through Bab el-Mandeb.

A Houthi attack on the Egyptian-owned cargo ship Tihamah in Bab el-Mandeb killed six people and wounded 10. These were the first shipping deaths linked to the Houthis since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February 2026.

The Houthi naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, aimed at Saudi ships and vessels calling at Saudi ports, took effect on 20 July 2026 at 1200 UTC. Clarksons reported an average of 31 transits a day over 25–26 July, and 33 transits were preliminarily recorded on 21 July.

Even during the worst Houthi attacks in early 2024, PortWatch showed daily Bab el-Mandeb transits staying in the 30–50 range, against a pre-crisis baseline of about 50 or more a day. This is a secondary summary and unverified against PortWatch's raw series.
The lowest weekly Bab el-Mandeb transit total of the 2023–24 Houthi crisis came in the week ending 10 March 2024: 218 passages, or about 31 a day. This is Lloyd's List's count, not PortWatch's.
Daily Bab el-Mandeb transits averaged 31 in the week ended 2 March 2026, compared with a normal level of more than 70. No source found shows a 7-day average near 10 at any point since 2023.

An earlier question in the same series asked whether PortWatch's 7-day average for Bab el-Mandeb would reach 10 or fewer transit calls by 30 September 2026. Recent weekly figures (about 38–41 a day) suggest it did not, but the PortWatch page could not be read directly to confirm.

The question resolves on PortWatch's AIS-based count of 'Arrivals of Ships' (transit calls) for Bab el-Mandeb, as a 7-day moving average. The threshold is 10 or fewer, roughly a 75% drop from the current level of about 40 a day. PortWatch data usually lag by several days, and data published up to 14 days after 31 October counts.
About 25 days remain until 31 October 2026. Any qualifying daily 7-day average from market creation through 31 October triggers YES; otherwise it resolves NO once data for 31 October is published.

market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Unnamed people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that the East-West pipeline is still running normally after reports of a new weekend strike on a pumping station near Khurais. Saudi Aramco and the Energy Ministry did not immediately answer Bloomberg's requests for comment. The 'operating normally' claim comes from those sources, not from the government.

Reports say that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Aramco has said anything publicly about the pipeline since it was attacked in September. Every report of a restart or higher flows so far comes from anonymous sources or market-intelligence firms.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia raised flows on the 7 million b/d East-West pipeline to more than 80% of capacity, close to 6 million b/d, with about 4.5 million b/d available for export. These figures came from tanker-tracking and market data such as Kepler, not from a government statement.

Anonymous Reuters sources said the pipeline restarted on September 22 at a low rate, with Aramco working to bring flows back to about 4 million b/d. The article cites no statement from the government or the Ministry of Energy.

The Ministry of Energy said in an official SPA statement that the East-West pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after several drone attacks on September 10 in the Riyadh and Medina regions. The ministry said teams were taking steps to secure the pipeline and assess its safety.
The Saudi Foreign Ministry condemned the attack, carried out by several drones from Iraq, saying it caused injuries and 'some damage that is currently being addressed.'

Precedent from earlier in 2026: after attacks in April cut flows on the East-West pipeline, the Ministry of Energy announced through SPA on April 12 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has publicly confirmed restorations before. This is a single case.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC the closure would be a short interruption lasting days. He is a US official, not part of the Saudi government, so his statement does not count toward resolution.

Sources gave different repair estimates: one said five to six weeks, another said sooner. After the September 22 restart, Reuters sources said getting back to full capacity would likely take at least six to eight weeks.

The question resolves Yes only if official Saudi government information says the pipeline is currently operating, at any capacity, by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Anonymous-source reports like the Reuters and Bloomberg pieces do not count, and neither do statements about future or planned resumption. Based on what was found, no qualifying government statement has been reported as of October 5.

About 26 days remain before the deadline (October 31, 11:59 PM ET; the question closes November 1, 03:59 UTC). No scheduled ministry briefing on the pipeline was found. Attacks are continuing, including the reported strike near Khurais on the weekend of October 3–4.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Saudi-Houthi ceasefire agreement announced by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a ceasefire agreement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A ceasefire agreement refers to any mutually-agreed suspension of direct military engagement between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, political framework, truce, or humanitarian pause will qualify if it includes a mutually agreed suspension of direct military engagement, to be effective on a specified date. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify. Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered a ceasefire agreement. Only agreements which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Agreements which only apply to specific conflict categories (e.g. restrictions on certain target categories or certain locations) will not qualify.

All listed countries/parties must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for a Yes resolution. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.

Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a ceasefire agreement will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where a potentially qualifying announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a ceasefire agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries/parties or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 7 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the seventh calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, the announcements will be judged based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia and Houthi leadership; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

A Maariv poll found that an Eisenkot-led opposition could reach 61 seats without Arab parties if the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists-Economic slate (4 seats) joined it. In that poll Winter's party fell below the threshold.

Netanyahu leads the outgoing 37th government. The 25th Knesset dissolved on its scheduled date, July 17, 2026, after serving its full four-year term. Likud is running merged with New Hope, and Bennett and Lapid are running together on the 'Together' list.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $105 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: Front-month WTI crude was at $89.08/bbl on October 5, 2026, down $2.03 (-2.23%) on the day, with an intraday low of $88.93. It was down 4.25% over the month and up 44.4% year on year.

NYMEX Nov'26 WTI expires October 20, 2026. Under the ICE rule (5 US business days before the 25th, because Oct 25 is a Sunday), ICE Nov WTI's last trade would be about Oct 19. WTI settled at $91.11 on Friday, October 2, down $1.76 from Thursday's $92.87 settlement. The drop followed a European agreement to release emergency diesel stocks under a G7/IEA plan of about 100 million barrels.
On October 1, WTI jumped nearly 3% to $92.87 after a U.S. aircraft carrier deployment. EnergyNow also cited China's suspension of fuel exports and renewed U.S.-Iran military concerns that day.

Oil fell on October 5 as Middle East crude exports rose and the G7 released about 100 million barrels of reserves. Higher loadings through the Strait of Hormuz and continued operation of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline eased supply concerns. Brent was about $102.40 and WTI about $90.65.

Saudi Aramco cut its November Arab Light price to Asia to $5 below the regional benchmark as Middle Eastern flows normalize. Saudi-backed forces in Yemen launched operations against Houthi areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and OPEC+ kept quotas unchanged.
WTI closed at $96.05 on September 9, 2026, its highest close since May 22. Oil rose more than 8% in September as the U.S. and Iran exchanged strikes.

WTI closed at $96.02 on June 3 after Netanyahu said the U.S. and Israel might strike Iran again. No WTI close at or above $105 appears in the June–October 2026 chronology.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.source: Faktor Plus via sd.rs / Wikipedia polling page
recent_facts.fact: Faktor Plus poll (Sept 16–20, 2026, 986 respondents) has 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' at 48.6% (+1.4 on the month) and the Student List at 37.1% (+5.6). SPS polled 4.9%, European Serbia 3.6%, Authentic Right 2.8% and Nestorović's list 1.2%. Expected turnout was about 62%, and 16% were undecided.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Opinion polling for the next Serbian parliamentary election)
recent_facts.fact: A CRTA poll from around July 15, 2026 (n=2,324) had the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7%. It was described as the first regular national poll since July 2010 in which an option other than SNS came first. NSPM in late July had the Student List at 39.6% and SNS at 37.5%.

Earlier Faktor Plus polls had SNS well ahead: 46.4% vs 28.7% in April, 47.1% vs 30.7% in June, and 47.2% vs 31.5% in early September 2026 (n=1,200). Faktor Plus has had SNS first in every poll, while CRTA and NSPM have had the Student List first.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency, using the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which is waived for ethnic-minority lists. Sixteen electoral lists are registered.

Vučić resigned as President on September 27, 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as candidate for Prime Minister. Ana Brnabić became acting president. The list's first three candidates are Vučić, Miloš Vučević and Ana Brnabić.
Vučić called early parliamentary elections for October 25, 2026, and the Assembly was dissolved on September 9. The elections were originally due by December 2027.

Registered lists include United Serbia (SNS-led, submitted Sept 12; ballot number 1), SPS-led 'Factor of Stability' (Sept 12), 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (Sept 14; ballot number 3) and the opposition coalition European Serbia (SSP–Serbia Centre–Solidarity, Sept 19). Some opposition parties withdrew to back the Student List.

CRTA's campaign monitoring reports that the Student List's lead candidate, Ilija Srdanović, has had no live appearances on national TV since the list was declared on September 15. Over the same period Vučić made 17 appearances, in which he portrayed the Student List as 'anti-Serbian' and acting on 'orders from abroad'. Vučić has called CRTA's polls propaganda, and CRTA says he is trying to discredit it as an election observer.

market.question: Will the Republican Party win the MT-01 House seat?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the MT-01 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

recent_facts.fact: In the Montana Free Press–Rutgers Eagleton poll of randomly selected registered voters (Aug 27–Sept 7, 2026), Republican Aaron Flint had 42% and Democrat Sam Forstag 41%. The margin of error was ±6 points, so the race is a statistical tie.

Public Policy Polling, sponsored by the Democratic committee The Bench, surveyed 536 registered voters on Sept 9–10 and found Forstag 45%, Flint 43% (±4.2 points). A NonStop Local News/American Pulse poll of 314 likely voters on Sept 19–24 found Flint 46%, Forstag 45%.
Cook Political Report moved MT-01 from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. Sabato's Crystal Ball also moved it from Likely Republican to Leans Republican.

Four candidates are on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot: Sam Forstag (D), Aaron Flint (R), Nick Sheedy (Libertarian) and Kimberly Persico (Independent). Incumbent Rep. Ryan Zinke (R) did not run for re-election, so the seat is open.
The Trump-backed No Going Back PAC spent $811,000 in September 2026 on the race. That included $743,275 on mailers opposing Forstag, mostly sent Sept 11–27.
Both the DCCC (Democrats' House campaign committee) and the NRCC (Republicans' House campaign committee) have put the open MT-01 seat on their target lists.
Forstag is running ads attacking Flint on health care and Medicaid expansion. The pro-Flint No Going Back PAC is running ads calling Forstag a lobbyist and attacking him on gender-related issues.

recent_facts.source: Helena Independent Record / Inside Political Money
recent_facts.fact: Flint and Forstag both reported raising more than $600,000 in earlier FEC filings. As of June 30, Forstag had raised $1.38 million in total, with 38% ($527,855) coming from donations of $200 or less.
Several Flint–Forstag debates are scheduled for October 2026. The general election is Nov 3, 2026, and third-quarter FEC reports are due Oct 15.
In 2024, Republican Ryan Zinke won MT-01 with 52.3% (168,529 votes) to Democrat Monica Tranel's 44.6% (143,783), a margin of 8.7 points.
In 2022, the district's first election after it was created in 2020 redistricting, Zinke beat Tranel 49.6% to 46.5%. Republicans have won both elections held in the district (2 of 2).
Trump won the district about 54% to 43% in 2024. Under the district's current lines, Trump beat Biden 52.2% to 45.3% in 2020.

On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba.
