market.question: Will the Republicans win the Maine Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Maine U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: As of Oct 4, 2026, the polling average listed on the page has Democrat Troy Jackson at 48.2% and Republican Sen. Susan Collins at 47.0%, with 4.8% other or undecided (Jackson +1.2).
Marist poll, Oct 1–4, 2026, 1,505 registered voters: Jackson 51%, Collins 47%. Trafalgar (R), Sep 29–Oct 1, 1,091 likely voters: tied 46–46.

Late-Sept/early-Oct polls: Wedgewood Jackson 52–48; CBS/YouGov tied 50–50; co/efficient (R) Collins 48–46; Maine People's Resource Center Jackson 49–47; InsiderAdvantage (R) tied 46–46; Fabrizio Ward/Impact Jackson 50–47; NYT/Siena (Sep 15–22) Collins 49–46; UNH Jackson 51–47.

Earlier polls had Jackson ahead by more: UMass/YouGov Jackson 48–43, YouGov Jackson 48–44, SSRS Jackson 48–45, Abacus Jackson 52–43, Rasmussen (R) Jackson 46–45. Since mid-September the race has looked closer.

Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary but withdrew on July 10 after sexual assault accusations. A Democratic nominating convention on July 25 chose former state Senate President Troy Jackson to replace him. The general election is November 3, 2026, under ranked-choice voting.
Independent candidate Tim Rich did not qualify for the ballot and independent Phillip Rench withdrew. The page shows Collins (R) and Jackson (D) as the main general-election candidates.
A pro-Collins PAC placed a $2 million ad buy attacking Jackson.

Reports say Collins has raised nearly $19 million and has $11 million cash on hand. Republican-aligned groups have booked about $62 million in ad time through Election Day, against about $23 million for Democrats.
Jackson raised about $7 million by mid-August after becoming the nominee. Because he trails in cash, his campaign is relying heavily on its ground game.
Four televised Collins–Jackson debates are scheduled: Oct 6 (WGME), Oct 8 (WMTW), Oct 13 (WABI/WAGM) and Oct 15 (News Center Maine/Maine Public/Portland Press Herald). Election Day is Nov 3.

Collins was first elected in 1996 and re-elected four times (2002, 2008, 2014, 2020), so she has won 5 of 5 Senate general elections. In 2020 she won by about 9 points while Biden carried Maine by about 9.

The question resolves Yes if the Republican nominee (Collins) wins, once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race; otherwise it falls back to official certification. Maine uses ranked-choice voting, so if no one gets a majority of first choices, the result depends on later tabulation rounds.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

“No longer under the control of the Houthis” means that the Houthis no longer exercise primary military control over Perim Island, and another state, occupying force, the internationally recognized government of Yemen, or an internationally backed authority has established control over the island.

Temporary raids, isolated landings, special operations, bombardment, sabotage, naval presence offshore, or temporary disruption of Houthi activity will not qualify on their own.

An announcement, threat, or claim that the Houthis have lost control will not qualify without actual control being established.

If control changes pursuant to a negotiated settlement, ceasefire term, surrender, or transfer agreement, this will qualify only once actual control has been established on the island.

If control over Perim Island is contested, unclear, disputed, or not sufficiently established by the resolution date, this will not qualify, and the market will resolve to “No”.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: Faktor plus's August–September poll (about 1,200 respondents) had SNS at 47.2%, the Student List at 31.5% and SPS at 4.9%. Its 26 June poll had SNS 47.1% and Student List 30.7%.
CRTA's 15 July 2026 poll (n=2,324) had the Student List at 44.9% and SNS at 35.7%. According to the page, this was the first poll since July 2010 to put any option other than SNS in first place.

All 250 seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency using the D'Hondt method. The threshold is 3% of votes and is waived for ethnic-minority lists, so the list with the most votes normally wins the most seats.

Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 Sept 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as its candidate for prime minister. He had called the early election in September 2026; parliamentary elections were otherwise due by December 2027.

RIK announced 17 electoral lists and one was withdrawn, leaving 16 lists competing for 250 seats. 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' is No. 1 on the ballot and 'Student List – Students Are Winning' is No. 3. Vreme describes these two as the dominant blocs in the polls.

The student movement submitted its 'Student List – Students Win' to RIK after thousands of supporters marched through Belgrade. The list has a full 250 candidates and is headed by Novi Sad cardiology professor Ilija Srdanović.

Controversies so far: fact-checkers documented pro-government tabloids using AI-manipulated photos against Srdanović; opposition parties and NGOs left a working group on improving election conditions, citing government obstruction; and the government has called the student movement a Western-funded 'colour revolution'. The 2023 election drew allegations of vote buying and transported voters.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 7 AM–8 PM at 8,210 polling stations for about 6.44 million registered voters. The voter-register and summary-list deadline is 9 Oct 2026.

recent_facts.fact: A Mainstreet Research poll released as the campaign entered its final month had Chow at 38.1%, Bradford at 32.2% and Alexander at 7.2%, a 6-point lead for Chow.

A Liaison Strategies Toronto Pulse poll had Chow ahead of Bradford 48% to 39% among decided and leaning voters, with Alexander at 10% and others at 3%. Chow's lead was slightly wider than in Liaison's previous poll, although her job approval had fallen below 50%.
An earlier Liaison poll had Chow at 47%, Bradford at 40% and Alexander at 10% among decided and leaning voters. Women backed Chow 56% to 32%, while men backed Bradford 47% to 41%.

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, the day advance voting began, Chris Alexander, a former Conservative minister who placed third, dropped out of the race. He endorsed no other candidate, and his name is likely to stay on the ballot.

Wikipedia's summary of the campaign polling says Chow has led Bradford in most polls, by 7 to 17 points. More than 60 candidates registered, and the main contenders are Chow, Bradford (councillor for Ward 19) and Alexander, who has now withdrawn.

Chow is endorsed by CUPE Local 79, LiUNA Local 183, the Toronto and York Region Labour Council and several NDP MPPs and MPs. Bradford is endorsed by Liberal MPs Yvan Baker and Judy Sgro, former MPs Peter Kent and John McKay, and musician Geddy Lee.
Advance voting began on Oct. 6, and election day is Oct. 26, 2026. The nomination period ran from May 1 to Aug. 21, 2026.

Toronto elects its mayor by first-past-the-post in a single round, so whoever gets the most votes on Oct. 26 wins and there is no runoff. Chow is the incumbent and is seeking her first full term after winning the 2023 by-election.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the Republican Party win the MT-01 House seat?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party of the candidate who wins the MT-01 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026.

​​A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time all of the 2026 House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democrat or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus at the time all of the House elections are conclusively called by this market's resolution sources.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the United States government, specifically the Federal Election Commission (https://www.fec.gov/).

recent_facts.fact: In the Montana Free Press–Rutgers Eagleton poll of randomly selected registered voters (Aug 27–Sept 7, 2026), Republican Aaron Flint had 42% and Democrat Sam Forstag 41%. The margin of error was ±6 points, so the race is a statistical tie.

Public Policy Polling, sponsored by the Democratic committee The Bench, surveyed 536 registered voters on Sept 9–10 and found Forstag 45%, Flint 43% (±4.2 points). A NonStop Local News/American Pulse poll of 314 likely voters on Sept 19–24 found Flint 46%, Forstag 45%.
Cook Political Report moved MT-01 from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. Sabato's Crystal Ball also moved it from Likely Republican to Leans Republican.

Four candidates are on the Nov 3, 2026 general election ballot: Sam Forstag (D), Aaron Flint (R), Nick Sheedy (Libertarian) and Kimberly Persico (Independent). Incumbent Rep. Ryan Zinke (R) did not run for re-election, so the seat is open.
The Trump-backed No Going Back PAC spent $811,000 in September 2026 on the race. That included $743,275 on mailers opposing Forstag, mostly sent Sept 11–27.
Both the DCCC (Democrats' House campaign committee) and the NRCC (Republicans' House campaign committee) have put the open MT-01 seat on their target lists.
Forstag is running ads attacking Flint on health care and Medicaid expansion. The pro-Flint No Going Back PAC is running ads calling Forstag a lobbyist and attacking him on gender-related issues.

recent_facts.source: Helena Independent Record / Inside Political Money
recent_facts.fact: Flint and Forstag both reported raising more than $600,000 in earlier FEC filings. As of June 30, Forstag had raised $1.38 million in total, with 38% ($527,855) coming from donations of $200 or less.
Several Flint–Forstag debates are scheduled for October 2026. The general election is Nov 3, 2026, and third-quarter FEC reports are due Oct 15.
In 2024, Republican Ryan Zinke won MT-01 with 52.3% (168,529 votes) to Democrat Monica Tranel's 44.6% (143,783), a margin of 8.7 points.
In 2022, the district's first election after it was created in 2020 redistricting, Zinke beat Tranel 49.6% to 46.5%. Republicans have won both elections held in the district (2 of 2).
Trump won the district about 54% to 43% in 2024. Under the district's current lines, Trump beat Biden 52.2% to 45.3% in 2020.

market.question: Will Bernie Sanders endorse James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026?
market.rules:
If Bernie Sanders publicly endorses James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
An endorsement requires a clear, affirmative statement of support for the nominee's election. The statement must be public (not private communications) and specifically reference the race or be clearly in context of the race. The endorsement must come directly from the person or through their official channels. Positive comments without explicit support, policy endorsements without nominee endorsement, or conditional endorsements do not qualify. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. Sarcastic statements or those immediately clarified as jokes do not qualify.

Republicans are using the Sanders comparison as an attack line. The exact date was not captured, so the date shown is when this desk found the article, not the publication date.
As of September 29, 2026, Jasmine Crockett's PAC had released new endorsements that still did not include Talarico.

Election Day is November 3, 2026, and the question closes at 15:00 UTC that day. About four weeks remain for Sanders to make an endorsement. A public statement or a quote tweet with supportive commentary from his verified account would count; likes, retweets or conditional praise would not.

(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: Israeli sources told CNN the co-pilot accused of trying to hijack the flydubai plane probably acted alone.
Officials said early signs point to the co-pilot acting alone. A senior US official briefed on Israel's investigation told NBC there were no signs that Iran directed or took part in the attack.

Co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami reportedly confessed, saying 'I did it as revenge for Gaza; I wanted to die as a martyr.' He reportedly planned to crash into Ben Gurion Airport and had a backup plan to target a US military base in Jordan. The report says Israeli officials hinted, without confirmation, that he had visited 'enemy countries'.
A joint UAE–Israel investigation is reportedly looking at the co-pilot's radicalisation during a stay in Syria and at a possible link to an Iranian-backed terrorist group.

PM Netanyahu said the co-pilot 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination' and that 'We'll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we'll find out very soon.' He also told Fox it was 'too early to say' whether Iran was involved.

Netanyahu pointed to Iran and its proxies as intent on stepping up attacks on Israelis abroad, but did not directly attribute the flydubai attack to them. The incident comes ahead of an Israeli election and during a US-Israel war against Iran that began in late February 2026.

US President Trump suggested the co-pilot may be linked to Iran 'based on what I'm hearing' but gave no details. This went further than Netanyahu's statements. Trump is not an Israeli official, so his statement does not count for this question.

National Security Minister Ben Gvir said the alleged attack shows Israel must step up its military campaigns across the region. Ministers called for more military action after the incident (Jerusalem Post), but neither report describes a minister saying Iran or a proxy carried out or directed the attack.

The UAE Attorney General called the attack a 'terrorist act' and said investigators are checking whether al-Hammami, an Omani national born in the UAE to a Syrian mother, acted as a 'lone wolf' or had links to extremist groups. Omani authorities had earlier barred him from flying over concerns about extremist views.
Netanyahu ordered a security review of flights to Israel after the flydubai attack.

In Game 2, Freddy Peralta retired the first 9 Yankees and allowed 1 run in 4 2/3 innings. Ben Rice tied it 1-1 with a 4th-inning homer, which was New York's first hit, but Tampa Bay went up 3-1 in the 5th. Cam Schlittler gave up 3 runs in 4 1/3 innings.

The Yankees made three defensive miscues in the first inning of Game 2: a McMahon error, a wild throw by Jazz Chisholm Jr. that let a run score, and catcher's interference on Austin Wells. That put Tampa Bay up 1-0 and pushed Schlittler to 19 pitches in the inning.

The Rays won Game 1 1-0 at Tropicana Field on Oct 3. Drew Rasmussen took a no-hitter into the 8th inning with 10 strikeouts and 2 walks before Austin Wells doubled with two outs. Jonathan Aranda's 3rd-inning homer off Gerrit Cole was the only run.
Remaining schedule: Game 3 at Yankee Stadium on Oct 7, Game 4 at Yankee Stadium on Oct 8 if needed, and Game 5 at Tampa Bay on Oct 10 if needed.

10 MLB teams have come back from 0-2 down to win a best-of-five series, about 11% of roughly 90 such series. The comebacks include the 2001 Yankees over Oakland and the 2017 Yankees over Cleveland, and the most recent was 2017. I could not confirm how many 0-2 series have been played since then (the total may now be above 90), so treat the exact rate as unverified.

The projected Game 3 Yankees starter was Carlos Rodón (tentative), who threw eight scoreless innings against Tampa Bay on Sept 22. The Rays listed Nick Martinez or Freddy Peralta for Game 3, but Peralta has now started Game 2.

Rasmussen went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA and an AL-best 0.91 WHIP, and has a career 1.81 ERA against the Yankees. Peralta was the AL Pitcher of the Month for September, going 5-0 with a 0.79 ERA over his last six starts. Schlittler finished with a 1.95 ERA, and Cole had a 2.50 ERA in three starts against Tampa Bay this season.

market.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

Election day is October 27, 2026, with voting at diplomatic missions on October 20. Surplus-vote agreements are due by October 16, and official results are to be confirmed on November 4, 2026. Candidate lists closed on September 8, 2026.

A late-September poll showed Eisenkot and Netanyahu tied, and Jerusalem Post headlines from that week described Likud and Yashar 'trading leads'. This shows the narrowing trend from the early-September polls, where Yashar was 3–4 seats ahead.

NLDS Game 3 is Oct. 6, Game 4 (if needed) is Oct. 7 and Game 5 (if needed) is Oct. 9. The NL bracket pairs Dodgers-Braves and Brewers-Padres, and the two winners meet in the NLCS.

The League Championship Series run Oct. 11–20 and the best-of-seven World Series runs Oct. 23–31, with a possible Game 7 on Oct. 31. The champion would be decided before the questions close on Oct. 31 at 23:55 UTC.
The Braves reached the NLDS by beating the Phillies 2-1 in the NL Wild Card Series, winning the deciding Game 3 6-2.

In Game 2, Atlanta used reliever Ray Kerr as an opener; he got eight outs without allowing a run. 21-year-old Didier Fuentes allowed only a solo homer over four innings. The Dodgers managed just two solo homers, by Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman.
In the AL Division Series, the Rays face the Yankees and the White Sox face the Guardians. The Rays and White Sox each led their series 1-0 after Game 1; ALDS Game 2 is Oct. 5.

market.question: Will Ilija Srdanović be the next prime minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: An early parliamentary election for all 250 National Assembly seats is set for 25 October 2026, after Vučić dissolved the Assembly on 9 September. Seats are allocated by closed-list PR with d'Hondt and a 3% threshold, which is waived for minority parties. A majority is 126 seats.

Ilija Srdanović, a Novi Sad cardiologist and medical professor born in 1970, heads the ballot for the 'Student List – Students Are Winning' in the 2026 election. Reporting describes him as the Student List's lead candidate for prime minister.
Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026 to run for prime minister. He heads SNS's 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list.

Vučić launched his campaign for prime minister on 3 October at Belgrade Arena and promised a 'comprehensive' victory. Al Jazeera reports that if SNS wins a majority, parliament would elect Vučić as PM. It describes the Student List as the main challenger.
A Faktor Plus poll had Vučić's United Serbia at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%. That was a 5.6-point gain for the Student List.
An NSPM poll presented by Vukadinović had the Student List at 44.4% and United Serbia at 41.7%. The exact publication date is approximate: late September or early October 2026.
A CRTA survey found 44% of respondents backing the Student List and 32% backing Vučić's bloc. The publication date is approximate: September 2026.
Speaking from New York, Vučić was reported as saying the Student List leads and is 'hard to catch'.
Another poll had the Student List at 39.6% and SNS at 37.5%. Wikipedia sums up recent polling as a tightened race in which results vary by pollster.

Other lists include European Serbia (Tepić/Ponoš), Authentic Right (Miloš Jovanović) and the SPS-led Factor of Stability (Ivica Dačić). SSP said it would cooperate with the Student List. PSG dropped out of the race to back the Student List.
Election day is 25 October 2026, the same day this question closes. A PM can only be elected later, after the new Assembly holds its constitutive session.

After the 17 December 2023 election, the new Assembly first met on 6 February 2024 and the President named Vučević PM-designate on 30 March. The government was elected on 2 May 2024, about 4.5 months after the vote, with 152 votes in favour.

Under Serbian procedure, the President gives the mandate to a PM-designate, and the Assembly then elects the PM and cabinet by a majority of all 250 MPs, meaning 126 votes. Vučić has resigned, so who will give the mandate after the vote is not confirmed in these sources (unverified).

market.question: Will Bernie Sanders endorse James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026?
market.rules:
If Bernie Sanders publicly endorses James Talarico in the 2026 United States Senate election in Texas before Nov 3, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
An endorsement requires a clear, affirmative statement of support for the nominee's election. The statement must be public (not private communications) and specifically reference the race or be clearly in context of the race. The endorsement must come directly from the person or through their official channels. Positive comments without explicit support, policy endorsements without nominee endorsement, or conditional endorsements do not qualify. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. Sarcastic statements or those immediately clarified as jokes do not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: Bernie Sanders does not appear on Talarico's endorsement list on the Wikipedia page for the 2026 Texas Senate race. The general election between Talarico (D) and Ken Paxton (R) is on November 3, 2026.

recent_facts.source: The Independent (via Politics & Poll Tracker on X)
recent_facts.fact: Sanders said he would campaign for Talarico in Texas if asked. He said Talarico 'stands an excellent chance to become the next senator from Texas' and that Texas has progressive potential. This is not an explicit endorsement. The date is estimated from the post ID, around the March 3 primary.
During the primary, after meeting with Talarico, Sanders said it was 'too early' to say whether he would endorse him.
Talarico won the Democratic primary outright with 52.4% of the vote over Rep. Jasmine Crockett and avoided a runoff. He is now the Democratic nominee.

Sanders has endorsed Angie Nixon, a Democratic Senate candidate in Florida, so he is making Senate endorsements this cycle. The exact date was not captured, so the date shown is when this desk found the article, not the publication date.
TIME reported that Democrats in top Senate races call themselves capitalists. Talarico told TIME 'I am a capitalist' and rejected Republican efforts to label him a socialist.
Paxton has called Talarico 'a clear Democratic socialist.' Talarico responded by challenging Paxton to a debate on Fox News.

Sen. Ted Cruz said on his podcast that Talarico would be 'the most woke left-wing senator' and would model himself after Bernie Sanders. Republicans are using the Sanders comparison as an attack line. The exact date was not captured, so the date shown is when this desk found the article, not the publication date.
As of September 29, 2026, Jasmine Crockett's PAC had released new endorsements that still did not include Talarico.

Election Day is November 3, 2026, and the question closes at 15:00 UTC that day. About four weeks remain for Sanders to make an endorsement. A public statement or a quote tweet with supportive commentary from his verified account would count; likes, retweets or conditional praise would not.

market.question: Will Brad Bradford win the 2026 Toronto mayoral election?
market.rules:
The 2026 Toronto mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 26, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Toronto as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Toronto.

recent_facts.fact: A Mainstreet Research poll released as the campaign entered its final month had Chow at 38.1%, Bradford at 32.2% and Alexander at 7.2%, a 6-point lead for Chow.

A Liaison Strategies Toronto Pulse poll had Chow ahead of Bradford 48% to 39% among decided and leaning voters, with Alexander at 10% and others at 3%. Chow's lead was slightly wider than in Liaison's previous poll, although her job approval had fallen below 50%.
An earlier Liaison poll had Chow at 47%, Bradford at 40% and Alexander at 10% among decided and leaning voters. Women backed Chow 56% to 32%, while men backed Bradford 47% to 41%.

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, the day advance voting began, Chris Alexander, a former Conservative minister who placed third, dropped out of the race. He endorsed no other candidate, and his name is likely to stay on the ballot.

Wikipedia's summary of the campaign polling says Chow has led Bradford in most polls, by 7 to 17 points. More than 60 candidates registered, and the main contenders are Chow, Bradford (councillor for Ward 19) and Alexander, who has now withdrawn.

Chow is endorsed by CUPE Local 79, LiUNA Local 183, the Toronto and York Region Labour Council and several NDP MPPs and MPs. Bradford is endorsed by Liberal MPs Yvan Baker and Judy Sgro, former MPs Peter Kent and John McKay, and musician Geddy Lee.

Bradford promised to scrap the municipal land transfer tax on homes under $1.1 million, a measure he puts at $300 million, with buyers saving up to $18,000. He also promised to cut water bills by 25%.
Advance voting began on Oct. 6, and election day is Oct. 26, 2026. The nomination period ran from May 1 to Aug. 21, 2026.

Toronto elects its mayor by first-past-the-post in a single round, so whoever gets the most votes on Oct. 26 wins and there is no runoff. Chow is the incumbent and is seeking her first full term after winning the 2023 by-election.

recent_facts.source: Unverified (recalled from memory, not from a cited source)
recent_facts.fact: UNVERIFIED and based on very few cases: since the 1998 amalgamation, every incumbent Toronto mayor who ran for re-election has won (Lastman in 2000, Miller in 2006, Tory in 2018 and 2022), about 4 of 4.

Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

market.question: Will the rate of CPI inflation be above 3.6% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 3.6%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 3.6% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the
government shutdown

recent_facts.fact: The September 2025 CPI-U index was 324.800, up 3.0% over 12 months and up 0.3% for the month before seasonal adjustment. This is the year-ago base. Derived from the BLS levels: September 2026 needs an index of at least about 336.33 (up about 0.40% unadjusted from August) to round to 3.6%, and at least about 336.66 (up about 0.50%) to round to 3.7%.
BLS plans to release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA's weekly national average gasoline price rose through September 2026: $4.14 on Sept 3, $4.27 on Sept 10, $4.43 on Sept 17 and $4.48 on Sept 24. AAA called Sept 24 the highest ever for that time of year. On Sept 17 it was more than $1 above a year earlier.

AAA said the September 2026 monthly average was a record for the month at $4.33, 50 cents above the previous September record. It blamed Strait of Hormuz volatility and high crude prices. By October 1 the average had dropped nearly 7 cents to $4.41, and it was $4.365 on October 5.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). One search summary put the August monthly average at $4.19, which doesn't fit with these weekly figures, so that number is unverified.

Headline CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, up from 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3% after 0.2% in July. The gasoline index rose 3.9% in August, more than a third of the monthly all-items increase. Annual inflation stayed at 3.4%, the same as July.

The headline 12-month change BLS reports is calculated from not seasonally adjusted index levels and rounded to one decimal. So the September 12-month figure depends on the unadjusted August-to-September change, not the seasonally adjusted monthly figure.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $80 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.rules:

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS's August 2026 CPI release shows core CPI (all items less food and energy) up 2.4% over the 12 months to August 2026, not seasonally adjusted. It rose 0.3% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, after 0.2% in July.

Unrounded, August 2026 core CPI was +0.29% month over month, and the 2.4% year-over-year rate was described as the lowest core rate since March 2021. Core goods were +0.68% y/y and core services +3.01% y/y.
Monthly seasonally adjusted core CPI changes in 2026: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%.

Year-over-year core CPI in 2026: Jan 2.5%, Feb 2.5%, Mar 2.6%, Apr 2.8%, May 2.9%, Jun 2.6%, Jul 2.5%, Aug 2.4%. Nov and Dec 2025 were 2.6%, and there is no October 2025 reading because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (Sept 2025 CPI release archive)
recent_facts.fact: Base effect: the unadjusted core CPI index was 329.970 in August 2025 and 330.804 in September 2025, a non-seasonally-adjusted rise of about 0.25%. To print above 2.4% (2.5% or higher when rounded), September 2026's unadjusted core index must be at least about 338.91 (330.804 × 1.0245).
Core CPI rose 0.2% seasonally adjusted in September 2025, after 0.3% in each of July and August 2025. That September 2025 month drops out of the 12-month window in the September 2026 reading.
In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% (3.0% y/y), owners' equivalent rent rose 0.19% m/m (about 3.08% y/y) and primary rent rose 0.17% m/m (2.75% y/y). Headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y.
BLS will release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the question closes at 12:25 UTC that day.

market.question: Will **real GDP** increase by more than 2.0% in Q3 2026? (Above 2.0%)

recent_facts.fact: On October 1, 2026, the GDPNow nowcast for Q3 2026 real GDP growth (SAAR) was 3.7%, the same as on September 30. Its components included real PCE growth of 3.3% and real gross private domestic investment growth of 21.4%. The next update is Tuesday, October 6.

On September 30, GDPNow's Q3 nowcast fell to 3.7% from 5.0% on September 25. Its PCE growth nowcast dropped from 4.2% to 3.5%, which outweighed an investment nowcast that rose from 18.7% to 20.7%. Net exports were nowcast to subtract 2.60 percentage points.
Over the quarter the GDPNow Q3 2026 nowcast started at 5.0% in late July, was 4.4% on September 10, rose to 5.1% on September 16–17, and was 5.0% on September 25.

recent_facts.source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Nowcast (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: In early October 2026 the New York Fed Staff Nowcast for 2026:Q3 GDP growth was 2.2%, down 0.3 percentage point after new data releases. It had been 2.3% in late September. The exact date was not confirmed because the page did not render.
For Q2 2026, GDPNow's final nowcast was 1.5% and the BEA advance estimate was also 1.5%, matching after rounding. This is a single quarter, so it is unverified as a general accuracy rate.
Real PCE rose 0.6% (month over month) in August 2026, and nominal PCE rose 0.9%, the most since March. July's nominal PCE gain was revised down to 0.1%.

The July 2026 goods and services trade deficit was $88.6 billion, up $17.4 billion from $71.2 billion in June. Exports fell $6.6 billion to $310.7 billion and imports rose $10.8 billion to $399.3 billion.

In the third estimate, Q2 2026 real GDP grew at a 2.2% annual rate, revised up 0.7 point from 1.5%. Q1 2026 growth was 2.5%. The release included the 2026 annual update, which revised data from Q1 2021 through Q1 2026.

The BEA will release the Q3 2026 GDP Advance Estimate on October 29, 2026 at 8:30 AM, along with September Personal Income and Outlays. The August trade report comes out October 6, and the Q3 second estimate is due November 25.
A continuing resolution signed September 2, 2026 funds the federal government through December 11, 2026, so no shutdown should interrupt BEA's October 29 release.

market.question: Baycurrent Classic: Hideki Matsuyama wins
market.rules:
If Hideki Matsuyama wins the Baycurrent Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: Wyndham Clark is in the Baycurrent Classic field at Yokohama Country Club (par 71, 7,322 yards). At world No. 5 he is the top-ranked golfer in the field, and he has won three times this season, including his second U.S. Open.
Clark has published tee times for the 72-man field: Round 1 at 10:24 JST and Round 2 at 08:18 JST, playing both rounds with Justin Thomas and Adam Scott.
The Baycurrent Classic is a 72-hole, no-cut event with a 72-player field, an $8 million purse and 500 FedExCup points. If Clark withdraws or doesn't tee off, the winner market resolves No.

Golf Channel airs the event Wednesday to Saturday, 11 p.m. to 3 a.m. ET, which means the four rounds are played Thursday to Sunday in Japan, Oct 8–11, 2026. The tournament will be over well before the question closes on Oct 25.

The field includes 16 players ranked inside the OWGR top 50. Among them are defending champion Xander Schauffele (world No. 10), 2023 winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley and recent Biltmore Championship winner Jacob Bridgeman.

In his previous start, the Presidents Cup at Medinah, Clark went 1-4-0 and lost his Sunday singles match to Tom Kim 3&2. The U.S. still won 17-13. His total strokes gained was second-best on the U.S. team (this is a team event, so it is weak evidence about stroke-play form).
Clark won the 2026 BMW Championship, a FedExCup playoff event, finishing ahead of Rory McIlroy despite an even-par final round. Exact date not confirmed; it falls in the August playoff window.
Clark led the 2026 U.S. Open wire-to-wire for his second U.S. Open title. He also won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson in May 2026.
A season-stats summary covering 21 events (before his BMW win) showed 2 wins, 4 top-10s, 8 top-20s, 6 missed cuts and $9.86M in earnings, so his results this season have been uneven.

Past winners of the Zozo/Baycurrent event were Tiger Woods (2019), Patrick Cantlay (2020), Hideki Matsuyama (2021), Keegan Bradley (2022), Collin Morikawa (2023) and Xander Schauffele (2025). The 2024 winner was Nico Echavarria (from memory, not verified). In 2025, Schauffele won at 19-under, one stroke ahead of Max Greyserman.

No golfer has defended the title at this event. 2026 is only the second edition at Yokohama Country Club, so there is very little course history (1 prior event). The course was redesigned with new tees for 2026.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $110 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026? (copy)
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 3, 2026, the US naval blockade of Iran was still in force, and Trump was sending another aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Diplomacy was reported as deadlocked.

Preliminary tanker-tracking estimates showed Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It was the first such month since the war began in February.

Trump rejected Iran's 7-day proposal, under which Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade, removed oil sanctions and reinstated a regional ceasefire. Trump said Iran had 'overplayed their hand' but said he expected talks to resume that week.

On October 4, Iranian Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran was still reviewing a US counterproposal, sent through intermediaries. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said it was 'in line with their previous proposals concerning nuclear issues.' FM Araghchi said there is 'no military solution.'

The two sides disagree on what comes first. Iran insists the Hormuz and US blockade issues be settled first, while Washington insists on nuclear concessions. Qatar and other regional mediators are trying to revive the talks.

Trump said he was 'open to a deal, but not to the one the Iranians offered.' He reportedly told officials he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November 3 US midterm elections. The US also launched an expanded sanctions regime, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' in August 2026.

An IRGC advisor claimed that no US naval vessels are now in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz or the Gulf of Oman, and that US warships have pulled back 1,000 km. This is an Iranian claim; no official US announcement about the blockade accompanied it.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June MOU, including ending the naval blockade. Araghchi said the strait could reopen within seven days if those conditions are met.

Precedent: the first blockade ran from April 13 to June 18, 2026 (about 66 days). On June 14 Trump said he had 'authorized lifting the US naval blockade' once an accord was reached. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17, and CENTCOM announced the blockade's removal on June 18. That is one prior instance, so this is an unverified base rate.
The second blockade phase began July 14–15, 2026, after Trump's July 13 announcement, and was about 83 days old as of October 5. More than 100 vessels had been redirected by September 12.

No signed agreement or scheduled formal US-Iran negotiating session was reported before October 31. The next known date is the US midterm election on November 3, after which Trump reportedly expects renewed bombing.

Only an official, unambiguous US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts. Iranian claims, leaks, partial exemptions for specific vessels, and naval repositioning without an announcement do not qualify.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%. That makes 4.00% the upper bound going into the October meeting. It was the first hike since July 2023 and the first under Chair Kevin Warsh.

The September dot plot had a median of 4.1% for end-2026, which means one more 25 bp hike this year. 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026 and four projected two. The median showed no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028-2029.

The September statement cited persistent inflation, with core PCE above 3% in every month of 2026, and 'geopolitical developments'. Three members had already favored a hike at the July meeting. Only two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.
September nonfarm payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a consensus of about 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2%, and July and August payrolls were revised down by a combined 60,000.

Before the jobs report, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said labor market conditions 'have stabilized'. NY Fed President John Williams said there was 'no need for urgency' in deciding whether to follow September's hike with another.

Before the jobs data, Williams called another hike before year-end 'reasonable'. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack warned that inflation expectations could become entrenched after five years above target. Governor Lisa Cook said AI appears to be adding inflationary pressure and that the labor market 'appears to be well positioned to handle an increase in rates'.
At Jackson Hole in late August, Warsh said 'We have work to do' and suggested a rate hike in the coming months because of high inflation.

After the September jobs report, coverage shifted toward the Fed skipping October and possibly hiking in December. J.P. Morgan's stated base case is one more hike at the December meeting, and it notes that one argument for skipping October is giving the September hike time to work.
The September 2026 CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the main inflation release still to come before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

facts_dropped.fact: At his September press conference Warsh said 'Inflation is too high and has been for too long.' He said the hike was made because the committee was not confident that underlying inflation was moving toward 2% fast enough. Warsh did not submit SEP projections because he views them as forward guidance.
